blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
THE BIBLE, GOD'S WORD
Scripture Texts: Psalm 19:7-11; Psalm 119:89

The Bible used to have a larger place in the life of our people than now. It was read in many homes, used as an early school reader, studied, believed, and reverenced. Government leaders looked to it for foundation principles. Much literature contained Bible quotations. The Bible was read in schools, and passages from it were in reading books.

Gradually the Bible has been neglected. Fewer and fewer homes have family worship. Schools have dropped its use. As more Bibles lay closed, more people grow up ignorant of its teachings and indifferent to its authority. As a result, our nation has sunk to its lowest spiritual state. The Bible has the answer to every question and the solution to every problem that man faces today. God's Word is perfect in every way. It is genuine, authentic, and authoritative.
MEMORY VERSE: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand forever. —Isaiah 40:8
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 4:2-14 As the Lord commanded.
Tues.—Isaiah 59:16-21 God's Word is forever.
Wed.—Jeremiah 36 Punished for burning God's Word.
Thurs.—Ezekiel 33:21-29 God inspired Ezekiel.
Fri.—2 Thessalonians 2:1-13 Not man's word, but God's.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 19 God speaks to man.
Description of God's Word

Psalm 19:7-9 Five different names are given here by David to God's Word—law . . . testimony . . . statutes . . . commandment . . . judgments. Each adds a little different shade of meaning. He tells us it is perfect . . . sure . . . right . . . pure . . . clean . . . true . . . righteous altogether. It is sure—solid, strong, dependable. It is pure—unmixed. It is righteous altogether—no wrong or foreign bits in it. There are unbelievers who say the Bible merely "contains" the Word of God (along with many human words). No, it is the unmixed Word of God. It is right and good because God is good.
What God's Word Does

The Word of God blesses the whole man. Converting the soul—bringing salvation to it. Making wise— educates the mind. Rejoicing the heart—believing and obeying brings greatest joy. Enlightening the eyes—a Spirit-filled saint has a brighter look at life. Enduring forever—the saint who keeps the Word of God in the fear of the Lord will endure forever, living a strong and effective life.

Psalm 19:10-11 The wise, Spirit-filled one desires the Word of God. He has a real hunger and thirst for the Bible. He feels a need for it in his life each day. It is more precious than gold and sweeter also than honey. Gold speaks of value, honey of enjoyment. The Bible warns—shows the danger of straying from the right. In keeping of them—obedience—there is great reward, both here and in Heaven.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
A Settled Word

Psalm 119:89 Forever—eternally past, present, and future—God's word is settled in heaven. It is sure and changeless. Man cannot reach there to set it aside. He may reject or disobey it, but he cannot change it. The Word of God will change man, but man cannot change the Word of God. Read what happened to a man who burned God's Word in Jeremiah, Chapter 36.
Reason for the Bible

It is just natural that an all-wise Creator would communicate with His Creation. Would He make a world as complex as this, with many forms of life as well as the human mind and spirit, then abandon it without care or control? That would be unthinkable. He gave His Word to man in the Bible. It is a compass and chart to guide him along on his journey in this world.

The Bible, from beginning to end, recognizes that there is a definite and known Word of God. It shows itself to be that Word. Hundreds of times we read the word of the Lord came . . . God said . . . the commandments of God . . . thus saith the Lord, etc. It simply states this with no attempt to prove it, which is a characteristic of truth.
God reveals Himself to man through (1) nature, (2) the Bible, (3) Jesus, and (4) the Holy Spirit. The Bible is the path by which we are led to Christ and the Spirit.

The Bible is a collection of sixty-six Books, written by a number of authors, over about sixteen hundred years. The chief theme running throughout the Bible is the reclaiming of man from sin to eternal fellowship with God.

The Bible has two divisions—the Old Testament with thirty-nine Books and the New Testament with twenty-seven Books. The Old Testament tells of man's fall into sin and God's promise of salvation from it. It tells of God's choosing of a people for Himself through whom to send the Savior. To them, He gave the Law in preparation for salvation. The New Testament begins with the coming of the Savior and unfolds the plan of salvation to its culmination in Heaven. It tells of the gathering of a people of God—the church—to enjoy this salvation. The two Testaments are closely related. Almost all of the Old Testament was written in the Hebrew language. The New Testament was written in Greek. For people of other languages to read the Bible, it had to be translated into their languages. Any certain translation is called a version.
A Great Loss

All over the land are various moves for or against the Bible. When people lose the Bible, they open the door to all kinds of evil and invite God's judgments. We are losing the Bible in many cases. We must do all we can to bring it back. How can we do this? By using it and preserving it in our own individual lives. Put it back into our homes and lives. We may have to die for it yet. But isn't the Bible worth the cost? Many in times past considered it so.

This quarter's lessons accent the Bible with the purpose of increasing our knowledge of, love for, and obedience to, the Bible. But the Sunday school will never be enough to stem the tide of evil rolling across the land. Daily, personal home worship is necessary. Without it, we are saying by our example, "The Bible is not important." With it and obedience to it, we can arm ourselves with the strength of God. God grant that we do so.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is harder to crush a half-truth than a whole lie.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
WHAT THE OLD TESTAMENT IS
Scripture Texts: Romans 15:4; 2 Peter 1:19-21; 1 Corinthians 10:11; Exodus 19:5-6; Ezekiel 18:4; Isaiah 55:7

The history of the Bible is interpreted from the religious standpoint. Although the Prophets predicted certain events in the future, they were particularly preachers of righteousness and disclosers of God's purpose. From beginning to end, the Bible shows itself to be God's Book, our spiritual guide. The only thing greater than the Word of God is the Word made flesh. The whole testimony of the Bible points toward the coming of Jesus and fulfilling of His saving ministry among men.

The Bible is supernatural in nature. It is God's message to His children. The Old Testament is for our example and teaching. It tells of the curse of sin, the promise of a Redeemer, and the choosing of a people for His name. The Old Testament is thirty-nine Books, divided into five groups.
MEMORY VERSE: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. —2 Peter 1:21
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Exodus 12:1-14, 40-51 The Lord delivers Israel.
Tue.—Nehemiah 2:1-9 Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem.
Wed.—Psalm 16 A song of trust and praise.
Thu.—Isaiah 53 The atonement of Christ foretold.
Fri.—Joel 2:12-32 Promise of forgiveness and the Spirit.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 119:1-16 Blessing of Word on a life.
Purpose of the Old Testament

Romans 15:4 In the preceding verse Paul speaks of Christ and His voluntary taking of suffering upon Himself for others. He applies Psalm 69:9 to Christ. Then—whatsoever things were written aforetime— former writings, or the Old Testament—all were written for our learning. These Scriptures are for us. They are not out-of-date, useless books. Learn from them. Feed on the patience and comfort found there. Believe the promises. Hope in them.

2 Peter 1:19-21 The prophecy—the message from God—in old time. This is the Old Testament. It came not . . . by the will of man—was not human thought. It originated with God. The Holy Ghost . . . moved . . . holy men of God to speak or to write these words. The Old Testament came from God that it might be as a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.

1 Corinthians 10:11 All these things—incidents of the journey of Israel to Canaan—happened . . . for ensamples to us. Us upon whom the ends of the world are come— the last dispensation before the end of time. The Old Testament is for us. Study it, not to observe the forms of the Law, but to learn God's way.
It Tells of a People of God

Exodus 19:5-6 Ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me . . . a kingdom of priests . . . an holy nation. This, God spoke to old Israel. But there were terms to be met if they were to be this people. If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant. Upon these same terms, we now can be God's special, peculiar people,

His church (1 Peter 2:4-10). Only we have a different covenant now, not to keep the Law, but to repent and believe on Jesus Christ.
It Tells of God's Forgiveness

Ezekiel 18:4 The soul that sinneth, it shall die. This is the unchanging Law of God. When Adam sinned, he let death into the world, death to both soul and body. The only escape is through Jesus Christ (John 1:29).

Isaiah 55:7 Escape from sin is by way of repentance—Let the wicked forsake his way—turn to Christ— return unto the Lord—gain the forgiveness of God—He will have mercy . . . he will abundantly pardon. This is God's wonderful plan of salvation always existing in His purpose, promised and begun in the Old Testament, fulfilled in the New. His plan is always the same in principle. Only the outward forms of it differ under different covenants.

The Old Testament begins a continuous story of the Bible. It is of a contest between Satan and God for possession of man whom God created. Ancient Bibles were written by hand on parchment of goatskins or sheepskins, and then rolled into scrolls. Our Old Testament is thirty-nine Books, divided into five groups. The Jews had the same material but combined them in different order, and in three divisions: the Law, the Prophets, and the Holy Writings or Psalms (Luke 24:44). We have glimpsed a few leading points in the Old Testament. Let us now look at the Books.
The Five Books of the Law

Genesis opens with the account of Creation. God looked at what He had made and found it very good. But the devil came and tempted man to sin and thus brought spiritual and physical death to all mankind. Sin increased until God punished by destroying mankind with a flood, saving only Noah and his family. Man's pride led him to plan the city and Tower of Babel. God again punished by confusing the language and scattering the people. Now God began to build a nation through whom to send a Savior and to give His Word to man. The Israelites became slaves in Egypt, a type of sin's bondage.

Exodus tells of God's miraculous deliverance from that slavery and the giving of the Law. He delivered by means of the ten plagues. At Mt. Sinai God gave the Law (writing with His own finger), and the tabernacle was built to God's specifications. All the provisions of God for Israel were types of God's later provisions for the church.

The only thing greater than the Word of God is the Word made flesh.
The whole testimony of the Bible points toward the coming of Jesus and fulfilling of His saving ministry among men.

LESSON 3
HOW THE OLD TESTAMENT CAME TO US
Scripture Text: Psalm 145:1-13

God began to give His Word to man by speaking to him. He spoke to man in all ages, giving personal commands. When ready to give a system of law for guidance over a length of time, He first spoke it (Exodus 20:1-19), then He wrote part of it with His own finger (Exodus 31:18), then commanded Moses to write thou these words (Exodus 24:4; 34:27), and Moses obeyed. All Old Testament Books were written as God led the writers to write (Jeremiah 30:2; Habakkuk 2:2; 2 Peter 1:21). With few exceptions, they were written in Hebrew on parchment and rolled into scrolls to make a book. These were copied by hand by scribes, an expensive and laborious task.
The Old Testament is God's Word, was written to stand forever, and is to be spread to all people.
MEMORY VERSE: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.—Isaiah 40:5
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—2 Kings 22 Hilkiah finds a Bible.
Tue.—2 Kings 23:1-25 Josiah obeys the Bible.
Wed.—Isaiah 40:1-11 God's Word and promise will stand.
Thu.—Isaiah 45:17-23 Message of salvation for all people.
Fri.—Psalm 119:17-32 Prayer for the blessing of God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 62 Whole world to know of salvation.
Praise Passed Along

Psalm 145:1-9 In this song of praise and adoration of the Lord, David expresses the desire of his heart that all people should know God and join in praising Him. This is God's will. (Read Numbers 14:21.) One generation shall praise thy works to another—each generation has a responsibility to pass the good news on and on to others. Men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts . . . they shall abundantly utter the memory of thy great goodness. How will they know these? Because the record—God's Word—has been passed on to them. (Read Isaiah 40:1-8.) David had only the part of the Old Testament which was written to that date.
How Will They Know?

Psalm 145:10-12 Thy saints shall bless thee. They shall speak . . . and talk. The saints can never keep the mighty works of the Lord to themselves, for of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh (Luke 6:45). Of what shall they speak? The glory of thy kingdom . . . thy power. Why? To make known to the sons of men—other people—his mighty acts— God's acts of power, of love and mercy. And the glorious majesty of his kingdom—salvation, His work in the hearts of men, His spiritual rule in the earth, the glory of His divine organism, the church, which unites men and God. The saints are to speak, to proclaim this to the world. To do this, they must have and pass on the Bible.
God's Will

Psalm 145:13 We see from this Psalm that God's will is that His Word, His message, be given to all men of every generation. His is an everlasting kingdom. See Isaiah 9:6-7. Therefore, His Word by which He rules

must reach to all generations. He has provided for its preservation. It has come to us because God willed it so, and certain people did His will.

God directed scribes to write by hand the Books of the Law. Some were Ezra, Baruch, and others (Ezra 7:6; Jeremiah 36:4). The book of the law was to be kept in the ark of the covenant of the Lord (Deuteronomy 31:26). The Books were to be read to the people (Joshua 8:34-35; Deuteronomy 31:9-13). This custom continued through the time of Christ and of Paul, reading weekly in the synagogue (Luke 4:16-17; Acts 13:14-15). God's Word was to be taught to the children (Deuteronomy 4:9; Deuteronomy 6:6-7, Deuteronomy 6:20-25). Kings were to have God's Book and to live and rule by it (Deuteronomy 17:18-20). Israel neglected and lost the Books at times (2 Chronicles 34:14-21), but God preserved them even through neglect, war, and exile.

The original Books were directly inspired by God and thus were perfect. A few errors occurred in copying. In Hebrew, differences between numbers were sometimes shown by only the addition of a dot or two or a slight variation in a line. A copyist could easily mistake one for the other, especially on worn scrolls. When comparing Hebrew copies, the Targums in Aramaic and the Septuagint in Greek, no disagreement in essentials is found. Most convincing proof that our present Old Testament is a trustworthy copy of the inspired original is the fact that Jesus used, quoted, and approved of it (Luke 24:27, Luke 24:44). God has ordained that His Word shall not pass away.
Translations

About three hundred years before Christ, some Jews settled in Alexandria, Egypt. As their children learned Greek, they needed a Bible in that language. About 285 B.C. the Septuagint Version (means seventy) was translated from Hebrew into Greek. This is the Bible that Jesus used.

When the Jews were captives in Babylon, they gradually learned to speak Aramaic. When the Hebrew Bible was read, the meaning would be given orally in Aramaic (or Chaldee). Later these translations were written and called Targums (meaning translations).

In the first six hundred years after Christ, some Jews spent their lives in copying the Old Testament Books to get the most perfect complete Old Testament possible. These men were called Masoretes (meaning to hand down). They took great pains to have every letter perfect.

Translations were made by different people from different manuscripts into many languages, including the Gospel of John in English. In A.D.1380 in England, John Wycliffe finished translating the whole Bible from the Latin Vulgate into English. This is the Wycliffe Version. All was done by hand. For opening the Bible to the people, Roman priests had him arrested.

In A.D.1456 printing was developed in Germany. Now copying the Bible was less difficult. But translating and distributing it was opposed by the Roman Catholic powers. In 1527 William Tyndale began to translate the Old Testament. Before he could finish, he was imprisoned, strangled, and burned at the stake. Soon after came the Coverdale Bible, edited by Myles Coverdale. Matthew's Bible was made by John Rogers. He combined Tyndale's translation and Coverdale's. For his work, he was burned alive in 1555 in the persecution under the Catholic "Bloody Queen Mary."

In 1604 King James I approved the making of a new version to silence discord over current versions. Much of the influence and beauty of Tyndale's and Coverdale's work is seen in it. It was published in 1611 as the King James Version. This remains the best and most-used English version.
JUST A THOUGHT
"Great souls have fed on great spiritual food." 

The saints are to speak, to proclaim this to the world.
To do this, they must have and pass on the Bible.
Psalm 145:13 We see from this Psalm that God's will is that His Word, His message, be given to all men of every generation.
His is an everlasting kingdom.
See Isaiah 9:6-7.
Therefore, His Word by which He rules
How The Old Testament Came To Us─Lesson3 must reach to all generations.
He has provided for its preservation.
It has come to us because God willed it so, and certain people did His will.
God directed scribes to write by hand the Books of the Law.
Some were Ezra, Baruch, and others (Ezra 7:6; Jeremiah 36:4).
The book of the law was to be kept in the ark of the covenant of the Lord (Deuteronomy 31:26).
The Books were to be read to the people (Joshua 8:34-35; Deuteronomy 31:9-13).
This custom continued through the time of Christ and of Paul, reading weekly in the synagogue (Luke 4:16-17; Acts 13:14-15).
God's Word was to be taught to the children (Deuteronomy 4:9; Deuteronomy 6:6-7, Deuteronomy 6:20-25).
Kings were to have God's Book and to live and rule by it (Deuteronomy 17:18-20).
Israel neglected and lost the Books at times (2 Chronicles 34:14-21), but God preserved them even through neglect, war, and exile.
The original Books were directly inspired by God and thus were perfect.
A few errors occurred in copying.
In Hebrew, differences between numbers were sometimes shown by only the addition of a dot or two or a slight variation in a line.
A copyist could easily mistake one for the other, especially on worn scrolls.
When comparing Hebrew copies, the Targums in Aramaic and the Septuagint in Greek, no disagreement in essentials is found.
Most convincing proof that our present Old Testament is a trustworthy copy of the inspired original is the fact that Jesus used, quoted, and approved of it (Luke 24:27, Luke 24:44).
God has ordained that His Word shall not pass away.
About three hundred years before Christ, some Jews settled in Alexandria, Egypt.
As their children learned Greek, they needed a Bible in that language.
About 285 B.C. the Septuagint Version (means seventy) was translated from Hebrew into Greek.
This is the Bible that Jesus used.
When the Jews were captives in Babylon, they gradually learned to speak Aramaic.
When the Hebrew Bible was read, the meaning would be given orally in Aramaic (or Chaldee).
Later these translations were written and called Targums (meaning translations).
In the first six hundred years after Christ, some Jews spent their lives in copying the Old Testament Books to get the most perfect complete Old Testament possible.
These men were called Masoretes (meaning to hand down).
They took great pains to have every letter perfect.
Translations were made by different people from different manuscripts into many languages, including the Gospel of John in English.
In A.D.1380 in England, John Wycliffe finished translating the whole Bible from the Latin Vulgate into English.
This is the Wycliffe Version.
All was done by hand.
For opening the Bible to the people, Roman priests had him arrested.
In A.D.1456 printing was developed in Germany.
Now copying the Bible was less difficult.
But translating and distributing it was opposed by the Roman Catholic powers.
In 1527 William Tyndale began to translate the Old Testament.
Before he could finish, he was imprisoned, strangled, and burned at the stake.
Soon after came the Coverdale Bible, edited by Myles Coverdale.
Matthew's Bible was made by John Rogers.
He combined Tyndale's translation and Coverdale's.
For his work, he was burned alive in 1555 in the persecution under the Catholic "Bloody Queen Mary."
In 1604 King James I approved the making of a new version to silence discord over current versions.
Much of the influence and beauty of Tyndale's and Coverdale's work is seen in it.
It was published in 1611 as the King James Version.
This remains the best and most-used English version.
"Great souls have fed on great spiritual food." 

When ready to give a system of law for guidance over a length of time, He first spoke it (Exodus 20:1-19), then He wrote part of it with His own finger (Exodus 31:18), then commanded Moses to write thou these words (Exodus 24:4; 34:27), and Moses obeyed. All Old Testament Books were written as God led the writers to write (Jeremiah 30:2; Habakkuk 2:2; 2 Peter 1:21). With few exceptions, they were written in Hebrew on parchment and rolled into scrolls to make a book. These were copied by hand by scribes, an expensive and laborious task.

lessons.title: HOW THE OLD TESTAMENT CAME TO US

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 4
WHAT THE NEW TESTAMENT IS
Scripture Texts: Matthew 1:1; Matthew 26:26-29; Mark 14:49; Matthew 16:18-19; Acts 1:8-9; Romans 1:11-12; 2 Peter 3:18

The New Testament is twenty-seven Books in five groups. Each of the four Gospels is named for the writer. All tell the story of Jesus' life, yet each with a little different view. Matthew wrote, showing Jesus to be the Jews looked-for Messiah and King. Mark wrote and showed Jesus as the Servant of the Lord, beginning with John preparing His way, His baptism, and moved with swift action through the episodes of His life. Luke wrote of Jesus as the Son of man, stressing His human side. His Book begins with the birth of John and Jesus and gives much detail throughout. John's Gospel is somewhat different. It contains deep spiritual thought. John wrote, proving Jesus to be the Son of God. Much is told of Jesus' birth, death, and resurrection. His life is our example, but His death is our salvation. By it, He provided the perfect sacrifice for sin. His resurrection made effective His death and assured our resurrection.
The New Testament is the good news of salvation from sin through Christ, the calling out of the church, and full victory to come.
MEMORY VERSE: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.—John 17:17
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Mark 16 Resurrection and ascension of Christ.
Tue.—Acts 14 Missionary work of Paul and Barnabas.
Wed.—James 4 Exhortations to the church.
Thu.—Revelation 21 A description of the church.
Fri.—Psalm 119:33-48 A prayer to delight in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 2 Teaching the church by letter.
A New Covenant

Matthew 1:1 The book of the generation of Jesus Christ. "Generation" here means birth, the entering into human life. Christ was always divine. He is from everlasting to everlasting, but He had to take on humanity. The process of His doing so is His generation. It is expressed in His name Emmanuel, meaning God with us (Matthew 1:23). He was the eternal God come to live with us, to be one of us. Why are the names of David and Abraham singled out? Because promises were given to them which Christ's coming fulfilled. A son of David was to sit upon the throne of David (Isaiah 9:7; Luke 1:32). To Abraham God said, In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed (Genesis 12:3).

Matthew 26:26-29 The purpose of Jesus' birth was that He might die—die to redeem mankind. In dying, He sealed the new covenant with His blood. He gave bread and grape juice as symbols of that covenant. This is my body . . . this is my blood of the new testament (or new covenant). The old covenant was also sealed by blood, blood of animals (Exodus 24:3-8). The New Testament is so named because in it God's new testament of grace is set forth—not on stone, but written on the heart. With this He began to set up the spiritual kingdom over which He would rule forever. Until . . . I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.
Prophecies Must Be Fulfilled

Mark 14:49 But the scriptures must be fulfilled. The Old Testament had to be fulfilled if God's Word was to be everlasting. The Old is promise, the New, fulfillment. The New was not yet written when Jesus was on

earth. When it says He did things that it might be fulfilled which was spoken, it refers to Old Testament promises.
The Kingdom Set Up and Empowered

Matthew 16:18-19 Jesus said, I will build my church. In all of His work, He was gathering material for His church. He was setting up His kingdom. From the first, He preached the gospel of the kingdom of God (Mark 1:14; Luke 16:16). The New Testament is a record of the birth, growth, activity, nourishment, and future hope of God's peculiar people, the antitype of Israel, His peculiar treasure under the old covenant (1Peter 2:9; Exodus 19:5). Jesus said, I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven (or Kingdom of God) to use on earth. It would be foolish to believe that Christ would give Peter keys to a kingdom that did not exist.

Acts 1:8 Moving on into Acts, we read of Jesus' ascension back to Heaven and His promise: Ye shall receive power from the Holy Ghost. Who was to come upon them? The result is Ye shall be witnesses unto me—unto Jesus—in all the world. The Book of Acts is the record of that power and witnessing. The Holy Spirit did come (Acts 2) and filled saints went forth as He led. This was the church going forth to build His kingdom.

The Acts is a history book written by Luke. It takes up the story where his Gospel left off. It is an account of the progress of the church from the ascension of Christ and descent of the Holy Spirit to Paul's imprisonment in Rome. It is the history of the spreading of the Gospel and planting churches amid miracles and persecution in Jerusalem and Palestine, Asia Minor, and Europe. The conversion and work of Paul figures largely. It teaches what God expects His church to be.
Paul's Epistles

Romans 1:11 Now come the letters of Paul to the churches. How were new converts to apply their new knowledge and experience to their lives? To explain doctrine and instruct in Christian living, Paul wrote thirteen, and possibly all, of these letters. (Hebrews is unsigned.) They are named for the churches or individuals to whom they were sent. They are rich in spiritual food. Paul expresses his deep desire: That I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, that he might take of the living water in his heart (John 4:10, John 4:14; Acts 9:17) and plant it in theirs to spring up and flow out in rivers of living water (John 7:37-39). Why? That ye may be established, be rooted and built up in Christ (Colossians 2:7). This is provided as we study his letters.

2 Peter 3:18 These are the General Letters or Epistles. They were written for the same purpose, to help saints to grow in grace—in the use of the power of God made available for our lives, and in the knowledge of our Lord—getting to know Him by living in Him.

The Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ to John of the things that the church would go through from its birth until Jesus comes back to receive it to Himself. It tells of the many enemies of the church, its battles and great victories. In Revelation 22:20 Jesus says, Surely I come quickly. John looked forward to this. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus. Are you ready?

He is from everlasting to everlasting, but He had to take on humanity. The process of His doing so is His generation. It is expressed in His name Emmanuel, meaning God with us (Matthew 1:23). He was the eternal God come to live with us, to be one of us. Why are the names of David and Abraham singled out? Because promises were given to them which Christ's coming fulfilled. A son of David was to sit upon the throne of David (Isaiah 9:7; Luke 1:32). To Abraham God said, In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed (Genesis 12:3).

paragraphs.text: Matthew 26:26-29 The purpose of Jesus' birth was that He might die—die to redeem mankind. In dying, He sealed the new covenant with His blood. He gave bread and grape juice as symbols of that covenant. This is my body . . . this is my blood of the new testament (or new covenant). The old covenant was also sealed by blood, blood of animals (Exodus 24:3-8). The New Testament is so named because in it God's new testament of grace is set forth—not on stone, but written on the heart. With this He began to set up the spiritual kingdom over which He would rule forever. Until . . . I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.

paragraphs.text: The Acts is a history book written by Luke. It takes up the story where his Gospel left off. It is an account of the progress of the church from the ascension of Christ and descent of the Holy Spirit to Paul's imprisonment in Rome. It is the history of the spreading of the Gospel and planting churches amid miracles and persecution in Jerusalem and Palestine, Asia Minor, and Europe. The conversion and work of Paul figures largely. It teaches what God expects His church to be.

paragraphs.text: Romans 1:11 Now come the letters of Paul to the churches. How were new converts to apply their new knowledge and experience to their lives? To explain doctrine and instruct in Christian living, Paul wrote thirteen, and possibly all, of these letters. (Hebrews is unsigned.) They are named for the churches or individuals to whom they were sent. They are rich in spiritual food. Paul expresses his deep desire: That I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, that he might take of the living water in his heart (John 4:10, John 4:14; Acts 9:17) and plant it in theirs to spring up and flow out in rivers of living water (John 7:37-39). Why? That ye may be established, be rooted and built up in Christ (Colossians 2:7). This is provided as we study his letters.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 5
HOW THE NEW TESTAMENT CAME TO US
Scripture Texts: Colossians 4:16; 2 Peter 1:1; 2 Peter 1:12-15

The New Testament was written in Greek. For people of other tongues to read it, it had to be translated into their languages. Some languages possess many versions, and more than twelve hundred languages possess at least part of the Bible. Still others have none of it.

God gave the Bible. He desires all men to hear it, commanded that it be preached in all the world, and plants in the hearts of the saints a desire to tell it. He says it will never be destroyed but will accomplish the purpose for which it is sent. He exhorts us to search the Scriptures and to have His Words abiding in us. He has used His Word to bless and save millions. He will not allow it to be brought to an end. He is watching to guard against its destruction or corruption. We must do the same.
The New Testament is to stand forever and is to be passed on to all people for their salvation and spiritual nurture.
MEMORY VERSE: And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.—2 Timothy 2:2
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 7:37-46 Jesus cries His invitation to all.
Tue.—John 21:15-22 Christ's sheep must be fed.
Wed.—Acts 4:1-22 Apostles' passion for telling the news.
Thu.—1 Corinthians 9:16-27 Paul's passion to preach Gospel.
Fri.—Psalm 119:49-64 David's trust in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: 2 Timothy 2:1-10 Word is to be passed on.
Congregations Shared the Epistles

Colossians 4:16 Paul wrote this letter from his prison cell to the church at Colosse (Colossians 4:18). He tells them to cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans. Also, ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea. (Not written from there, but brought from there for reading.) Churches copied and kept the precious letters. They were written to be shared.

2 Peter 1:1 Peter wrote to the church in general—to them that have obtained like precious faith. Other books are addressed to saints generally: James—to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad; 1 Peter—to the strangers scattered throughout named areas; Jude—to them that are sanctified. Hebrews 3:1—Holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling. Christ gave The Revelation to shew unto his servants . . . 1 Corinthians—with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ; 2 Corinthians—with all the saints which are in all Achaia; Ephesians—and to the faithful in Christ Jesus. Three of the Gospels were recorded unaddressed for whosoever will to read. These show God's constant purpose to send His Word to all mankind. He puts His power behind its preservation and spread.
Plans for Preserving the Scriptures

2 Peter 1:12-15 Peter intended to put the church in remembrance of the need of diligent obedience to Christ. He did so even though the saints knew this and were established in the present truth—the level of truth given men in this present dispensation. He knew, from his own experience, how easy it is to fall (Matthew 26:69-75). Peter must continually remind each one as long as I am in this tabernacle—while I live in this

temporary body. Shortly I must put off this my tabernacle—die. How did he know? Our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me. But Peter's purpose of teaching God's Word reached beyond his death. I will endeavour that ye may be able after my decease to have these things—teachings, truths—always in remembrance. He preserved them in writing. No doubt, copies were made to keep in several safe places. Now over nineteen hundred years later we have Peter's letters. Other writers carried out God's plan to hand down their letters for our spiritual nutrition.
The Cost of Bringing the Bible to Us

Jerome spent twenty-one years in a monastery at Bethlehem translating a Greek Old Testament and an Old Latin New Testament to make the Latin Vulgate Bible. Some copies were brought to England for use of church leaders. The Christian king, Alfred the Great, who ruled from 871 to 901, encouraged righteousness and began his list of laws with the Ten Commandments and other Bible selections. After a long time, John Wycliffe translated the Bible from the Vulgate into Middle English, finishing in 1382. A group of men called Lollards (poor priests) copied Wycliffe's Bible and walked about England reading it to the people and teaching them to obey it.

After printing was invented, William Tyndale went to Germany to be free to translate and print the Bible. His first New Testaments, printed in English, reached England by smuggling in bags of grain and bolts of cloth in 1526. When strangled and burned in 1536, his last words were, "Lord, open the King of England's eyes." Three years later King Henry VIII ordered that English Bibles be used in churches. Seventy years later King James I ordered that a new translation be made. It was finished in 1611 and is the King James Version in use today in England, America, and elsewhere. Copies were placed in church buildings, sometimes chained to a desk where people came to read.

For translating the Bible, Wycliffe was arrested. His Bible was forbidden to the people. Church leaders severely punished them for owning, reading, memorizing, or teaching the Bible in English. Some paid the equivalent of $400 for a copy of it or a load of hay for a few chapters or for the privilege of reading it for a day. Years after his death, Wycliffe's body was dug up, burned, and the ashes strewed on the River Swift. Think of the long days and years spent in copying each Bible by hand, of the weary miles walked by the Lollards, and of the courage required of many to keep on in spite of persecution. A whole printing of Tyndale's Bible was publicly burned by order of the Bishop of London. Tyndale was put to death when only 44. This is but a small part of the cost of bringing the Bible to us. Yet it lies on the shelf in many homes, dusty and unread. Are we using it and obeying it as God intended? What of the future? Will it ever be a crime here to own and use a Bible?
JUST A THOUGHT
When we do what we can do, God will do what we cannot do.

Tyndale was put to death when only 44.
This is but a small part of the cost of bringing the Bible to us.
Yet it lies on the shelf in many homes, dusty and unread.
Are we using it and obeying it as God intended?
What of the future?
Will it ever be a crime here to own and use a Bible?

lessons.title: HOW THE NEW TESTAMENT CAME TO US

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 6
THE CHARACTER OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Matthew 24:35; 2 Timothy 3:16-17; 2 Peter 1:21; John 6:63; John 12:48

God has established methods by which He communicates with His creation, man, to tell him His will. Some of His methods are through nature, by direct speaking, by Christ, by the Holy Spirit, and through the Bible.

Nature speaks of God's power and majesty, but it cannot tell us who He is, whether He loves us, whether He will answer prayer, what the future holds, what our duty is, or anything of grace and atonement. We may see God in nature, but we cannot reach Him there. (Read Psalm 19:1-3.) God's most universal and plain communication with man is the Bible.

We have seen the important position occupied by the Church of God. If it is to fill its place in God's plan, we must know what God's will is. God has given us a Book which contains all we need to know to be saved and to do His will on earth. This Book is the Bible. What is it like?
MEMORY VERSE: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.—Matthew 24:35
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Kings 8:54-61 Solomon's benediction.
Tue.—2 Timothy 3:10-17 The defense of the faith.
Wed.—2 Peter 1:12-21 The basis of true knowledge.
Thu. — 1 Corinthians 2:6-16 True wisdom the gift of God.
Fri.—John 12:44-50 A summary of Jesus' claims.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 19:7-14 The works and Word of God.
It Is Eternal

Matthew 24:35 My words shall not pass away. It is God's Word. It is inspired by God. It is true. The world and all in it was brought into being by the power of His Word. There hath not failed one word of all his good promise (1 Kings 8:56). God's Word was before this world came into being and will stand sure after it has gone. His Word can never be destroyed because it is true.
The Bible Is Equipment for Christian Work

2 Timothy 3:16 All scripture is given by inspiration of God. Paul here refers to the Old Testament Scriptures, but this may be applied to the New as well. The Bible sets forth eternal principles which could have been conceived only by God. Its message fits any age of the world. If obeyed from the heart, it will produce a new and clean character inside and out.

It is profitable for doctrine—it contains the doctrine of God which is the rule and standard of our faith. Any doctrine which cannot be proved by the Bible is not required of man to accept. It is the last court of appeal for religious doctrine. For reproof—it will reprove and rebuke the sinful life. It holds a high standard of moral living. For correction—The Bible is profitable in restoring every person to his proper place in life. It will correct our attitude and conduct if they are out of order. For instruction in righteousness—we need no creed books or discipline books to guide us into the rules of faith and practice. The Word is sufficient. The Scriptures were written for our learning and instruction, that we might know the will of God for us (Romans 15:4).

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 6

2 Timothy 3:17 That the man of God—saved people, saints—may be perfect—perfect in purity, clean, sinless—and thoroughly furnished unto all good works. Read Ephesians 2:10. God's Book is fitted to carry out His plan. We need the Book if we are to work the plan.
The Bible Is Inspired

2 Peter 1:21 Moved by the Holy Ghost—The Old Testament Prophets spoke as the Holy Ghost came upon them. The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue (2 Samuel 23:2). This is inspiration. It is the method by which our Bible came to us.

The very Words of the Bible came from God. They were only written down by man. No other book is like the Bible. No other is inspired by God, or comes from God directly. Inspiration is the Holy Spirit putting into a man's mind and heart the Words to say or write. Prophecy (God's Word to man) came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake . . . moved by the Holy Ghost. This is God's way of giving our Bible to us. Over and over, the Bible claims to be God's Word. This fact puts the obligation upon us to accept and obey it.

Jesus put His stamp of approval on the whole Old Testament, all the Bible that was written at that time. The Jews included all of it in the three divisions Jesus mentioned. He said, all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law . . . prophets . . . psalms (Luke 24:27, Luke 24:44). If Jesus says they are true, we can be sure of them. While Jesus was with His disciples, He had pointed in the Old Testament to predictions concerning Himself. Now that He has been crucified and resurrected, He assures them again that their faith in Him as the Messiah might be strengthened, that all things concerning Him must be fulfilled (Luke 24:44).
The Bible Is Life-Giving

John 6:63 The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life. The message of Jesus (and the Gospel as a whole) has a spiritual application, and the fleshly mind cannot comprehend it without the spirit of understanding given by the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:14). It is the Spirit of life that is in Christ Jesus that brings salvation to us and not the letter of the Law. We may be strict adherents to the letter of the Word and not have the Spirit within our hearts, and it would profit us nothing. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his (Romans 8:9).

The Bible was given to us to use. In it, we find statements of truth, warning when we stray, a standard to measure us and bring us back to the right way, and a teacher of God's will. It is to furnish us thoroughly unto all good works. No one, however educated and trained otherwise, is capable of doing God's work unless the Bible is in his heart and mind and hand. This does not mean leaders only, but all of us who have been created in Christ Jesus unto good works (Ephesians 2:10). All are to spread the Gospel. Shall the whole beautiful, eternal plan of God come to an end, fail, when it reaches us, just because we do not read, study, eat, and obey His Word, the Bible? It is tragic that just that is happening in many lives.
The Bible Will Judge Us

John 12:48 The word that I have spoken . . . shall judge . . . Christ and His Word (doctrine) are one and inseparable. If we reject the message of His Word, we have rejected Him. It is impossible to have the Spirit of Christ dwelling in us and reject the Word. His Word and doctrine will be the standard of judgment on that final day.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 7
PROPHECIES OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Deuteronomy 18:22; Isaiah 34:16; 1 Peter 1:10-12

The Prophets did not understand all they spoke. They looked for the fulfillment of the prophecy but never lived to see it fulfilled. But they believed it would come to pass. They wondered what it was and when it would come. This was puzzling because they had the prediction only. The things they prophesied in their time are being fulfilled in this Gospel dispensation through Jesus.

Prophecy is not true, does not come to pass because it is written in the Bible, but it is in the Bible because it is true and will come to pass. Every prophecy of the Bible has so far been fulfilled. This is one of the strongest proofs of the truth of the Bible. No prophecy shall lack its fulfillment. We find fulfilled prophecies all through the New Testament.
MEMORY VERSE: Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare: before they spring forth I tell you of them.—Isaiah 42:9
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 18:15-22 The true Prophet promised.
Tue.—Isaiah 46:5-13 The end from the beginning.
Wed.—Ezekiel 12:21-28 God's Word shall be done.
Thu.—Daniel 2:24-30 God revealeth secrets.
Fri.—Psalm 119:65-80 Praising God for keeping His Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 42:1-9 God tells of events ahead.
True Prophecies Come to Pass

Deuteronomy 18:22 When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord—claims to speak for the Lord, to tell what God has told him. There were false prophets then as well as now. How can one tell the false from the true? If the thing follow not—if his saying does not come true, does not come to pass—then the Lord hath not spoken it. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously—without authority, without Word from God. Thou shalt not be afraid of him, shall not believe or observe his words. Implied here is the fact that prophecies which the Lord HAS spoken do come to pass, do occur just as spoken. No one is really a prophet unless God has spoken the message to him. We have a good example of this is 2 Samuel 18:19-31.

Jeremiah prophesied the captivity and death of Zedekiah, king of Judah (Jeremiah 34:1-7). The people accused him of disloyalty and put him in jail (Jeremiah 37:11-15, 28). But this (and other things) happened just as Jeremiah prophesied (Jeremiah 52:1-12). He spoke what God had spoken to him.
No Word of God Shall Fail

Isaiah 34:16 Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read. Read the promises, warnings, and predictions. No one of these shall fail. This is God's pledge. For every promise, there must be its matching fulfillment. Why? Because God's mouth it hath commanded. His Word cannot fail. His spirit it hath gathered them—the Spirit of God has gathered the Words, the people, and events together to bring the fulfillment. No Word of the Bible has ever been found false. God said He would bring all His Words to pass (Ezekiel 12:28).

LESSON 7
Old Testament Prophecies of New Testament Salvation

1 Peter 1:10-12 The prophets have enquired and searched diligently. They did not understand the meaning when they prophesied of the grace to come, so they enquired and searched for it. They wondered what it was and what manner of time it would come. The Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify— the Holy Spirit in their hearts made known these things. He testified beforehand—predicted— the sufferings of Christ, and the glory . . . For example, Isaiah wrote seven hundred years before Christ was born that He was despised . . . rejected . . . a man of sorrows . . . wounded . . . bruised . . . oppressed . . . afflicted . . . brought as a lamb to the slaughter . . . and was cut off out of the land of the living. All this for our iniquities. Then, in contrast, is the glory, that he shall see his seed . . . prolong his days . . . the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand . . . he shall be satisfied and divide the spoil with the strong (Isaiah 53). Puzzling, certainly, to one who has the prediction only. God answered their inquiries by revealing that they did minister the things . . . not unto themselves—the prophecies were not to be fulfilled in their time—but unto us in the next, this Gospel dispensation. The things they prophesied have come to pass and are reported by Spirit-led preachers of the gospel. They tell of Christ's substitutionary death, His Resurrection, and of those saved and Spirit-filled by His power. The prophecies of the old dispensation of Law are fulfilled in the new dispensation of grace. The angels are shut out from these blessings of salvation. They can only desire to look into them. They are precious to the angels, but only those who repent and believe can partake of it. Seek it, receive it, keep it, and tell of it.
Fulfilled Prophecies Prove the Bible
Some Old Testament prophecies and the fulfillment in Christ's earthly life are:
Prophecy Fulfillment
Born of a virgin Isaiah 7:14 Matthew 1:20-23
Born in Bethlehem Micah 5:2 Matthew 2:1
Healings Isaiah 53:4-5 Matthew 8:16-17
Riding into Jerusalem Zechariah 9:9 Matthew 21:4-5
Betrayed for silver Zechariah 11:12-13 Matthew 26:14-16; Matthew 27:3-10
Garments divided Psalm 22:18 John 19:23-24
Numbered with transgressors Isaiah 53:12 Mark 15:27-28
Railed upon Psalm 22:7-8 Matthew 27:39-44
Made intercession Isaiah 53:12 Luke 23:34

We can trust His promise to come again—John 14:3; Acts 1:10-11. These prophecies were given from seven hundred to a thousand years before Christ was born. That they could come true by chance is an absolute impossibility. No one man could by chance fulfill all these prophecies and more. Some of them no one not divine could ever fulfill. There is but one answer— the prophecies are from God, the Book is God's Book.
JUST A THOUGHT
There have always been unbelievers in God and His Word, but none have ever brought forth any proof.

memoryVerses.text: MEMORY VERSE: Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare: before they spring forth I tell you of them.—Isaiah 42:9

narrationUnits.text: The Prophets did not understand all they spoke.
They looked for the fulfillment of the prophecy but never lived to see it fulfilled.
But they believed it would come to pass.
They wondered what it was and when it would come.
This was puzzling because they had the prediction only.
The things they prophesied in their time are being fulfilled in this Gospel dispensation through Jesus.
Prophecy is not true, does not come to pass because it is written in the Bible, but it is in the Bible because it is true and will come to pass.
Every prophecy of the Bible has so far been fulfilled.
This is one of the strongest proofs of the truth of the Bible.
No prophecy shall lack its fulfillment.
We find fulfilled prophecies all through the New Testament.
Deuteronomy 18:22 When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord—claims to speak for the Lord, to tell what God has told him.
There were false prophets then as well as now.
How can one tell the false from the true?
If the thing follow not—if his saying does not come true, does not come to pass—then the Lord hath not spoken it.
The prophet has spoken it presumptuously—without authority, without Word from God.
Thou shalt not be afraid of him, shall not believe or observe his words.
Implied here is the fact that prophecies which the Lord HAS spoken do come to pass, do occur just as spoken.
No one is really a prophet unless God has spoken the message to him.
We have a good example of this is 2 Samuel 18:19-31.
Jeremiah prophesied the captivity and death of Zedekiah, king of Judah (Jeremiah 34:1-7).
The people accused him of disloyalty and put him in jail (Jeremiah 37:11-15, 28).
But this (and other things) happened just as Jeremiah prophesied (Jeremiah 52:1-12).
He spoke what God had spoken to him.
Isaiah 34:16 Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read.
Read the promises, warnings, and predictions.
No one of these shall fail.
This is God's pledge.
For every promise, there must be its matching fulfillment.
Why?
Because God's mouth it hath commanded.
His Word cannot fail.
His spirit it hath gathered them—the Spirit of God has gathered the Words, the people, and events together to bring the fulfillment.
No Word of the Bible has ever been found false.
God said He would bring all His Words to pass (Ezekiel 12:28).
1 Peter 1:10-12 The prophets have enquired and searched diligently.
They did not understand the meaning when they prophesied of the grace to come, so they enquired and searched for it.
They wondered what it was and what manner of time it would come.
The Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify— the Holy Spirit in their hearts made known these things.
He testified beforehand—predicted— the sufferings of Christ, and the glory . . .

For example, Isaiah wrote seven hundred years before Christ was born that He was despised . . . rejected . . . a man of sorrows . . . wounded . . . bruised . . . oppressed . . . afflicted . . . brought as a lamb to the slaughter . . . and was cut off out of the land of the living.
All this for our iniquities.

Then, in contrast, is the glory, that he shall see his seed . . . prolong his days . . . the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand . . . he shall be satisfied and divide the spoil with the strong (Isaiah 53).
Puzzling, certainly, to one who has the prediction only.

God answered their inquiries by revealing that they did minister the things . . . not unto themselves—the prophecies were not to be fulfilled in their time—but unto us in the next, this Gospel dispensation.
The things they prophesied have come to pass and are reported by Spirit-led preachers of the gospel.
They tell of Christ's substitutionary death, His Resurrection, and of those saved and Spirit-filled by His power.
The prophecies of the old dispensation of Law are fulfilled in the new dispensation of grace.
The angels are shut out from these blessings of salvation.
They can only desire to look into them.
They are precious to the angels, but only those who repent and believe can partake of it.
Seek it, receive it, keep it, and tell of it.
Some Old Testament prophecies and the fulfillment in Christ's earthly life are:
Born of a virgin Isaiah 7:14 Matthew 1:20-23
Born in Bethlehem Micah 5:2 Matthew 2:1
Healings Isaiah 53:4-5 Matthew 8:16-17
Riding into Jerusalem Zechariah 9:9 Matthew 21:4-5
Betrayed for silver Zechariah 11:12-13 Matthew 26:14-16; Matthew 27:3-10
Garments divided Psalm 22:18 John 19:23-24
Numbered with transgressors Isaiah 53:12 Mark 15:27-28
Railed upon Psalm 22:7-8 Matthew 27:39-44
Made intercession Isaiah 53:12 Luke 23:34
We can trust His promise to come again—John 14:3; Acts 1:10-11.
These prophecies were given from seven hundred to a thousand years before Christ was born.
That they could come true by chance is an absolute impossibility.
No one man could by chance fulfill all these prophecies and more.
Some of them no one not divine could ever fulfill.
There is but one answer— the prophecies are from God, the Book is God's Book.
There have always been unbelievers in God and His Word, but none have ever brought forth any proof.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 8
JESUS AND THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Hebrews 1:1-2; Luke 24:44: Matthew 5:17-18; John 6:63

The Gospels are biographies of Jesus. Acts is an account of the Spirit-led witness to Him by His church. The Epistles are records and explanations of His teachings. The Revelation is His showing forth of His plan for man from the beginning of the Gospel dispensation to eternity. Every Book of the Bible speaks of Jesus by promise or type or symbol or statement of fact.

Jesus is the central figure of the whole Bible. The Old Testament looks forward to Him; the New Testament looks back to Him. Both exalt Him. It is accurate to say Jesus "believed" the Bible. It originated with Him. Jesus recommends the Bible to be trustworthy when He quotes it, fulfills its prophecies, and tells us to search the Scriptures.
MEMORY VERSE: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me. ─John 5:39
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 5:36-47 Moses wrote of Christ.
Tue.—John 6:51-63 We must eat the Words of Christ.
Wed.—1 Timothy 6:3-14 God's Word is the foundation.
Thu.—Revelation 19:11-16 Jesus is the living Word of God.
Fri.—Psalm 119:81-96 Choosing God's Word in trouble.
Devotional Reading: Luke 24:13-32 All the Scriptures tell of Christ.
Jesus Is the Living Bible

Hebrews 1:1-2 In time past—in the former dispensation— God spoke unto the fathers by the prophets. In 2 Kings 17:13, we read that the Lord testified against Israel, or gave them no excuse, by all the prophets . . . saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments . . . according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets. The Prophets gave warnings, promises, teachings, commands, guidance, and foretelling of events. But now in these last days— the last dispensation of time—God has spoken unto us by his Son—Jesus Christ.

The Bible opens with the account of Creation, and the Hebrew word for God in Genesis 1:1 is plural (Gods). Jesus, together with His Father and the Spirit, created all things (Colossians 1:16). By whom also he made the worlds (Hebrews 1:2). He is the One promised to bruise the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15) and to bless the world through Abraham (Genesis 12:3). He is the Prophet promised to Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15). He is pictured as the Passover Lamb (Exodus 12). He is typified in Isaac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua, David, and others. The Psalms have many prophetic references to Jesus. For example, Psalm 96. The Books of Prophecy promise His coming—Behold, the Lord God will come . . . He shall feed his flock like a shepherd (Isaiah 40:10-11).

God has always communicated with man. Prophets brought His message. Some obeyed, but more did not. Then God began His better plan, a new dispensation. He sent His best message, His Son Jesus Christ. Jesus is called the Word in John 1:1 and John 1:14— the Word was God . . . the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us—and in 1 John 1:1-2, That which was from the beginning, which we have heard . . . seen . . . looked upon . . . handled, of the Word of life; (For the life was manifested . . .)—and in Revelation 19:13— And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. God gave us His written Law that is powerful, and then His living Word Who is more powerful. The written Word shows us His will. The living Word gives us power to obey it. By His written Word, He comes to us. By His living Word,

LESSON 8
He comes inside of us. The written Word and the living Word always agree. They are joined in one. The written Word, the Bible, proceeds from the living Word, Jesus Christ.
Jesus Said That the Bible Tells of Him

Luke 24:44 After His Resurrection, Jesus explained His death to His troubled disciples. All things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. Law, Prophets, Psalms— the three parts into which the Jews divided the Old Testament. Therefore, the Old Testament tells of Jesus. And Jesus presented it as true. We need no further proof. The night before His death, He said, The Son of man goeth as it is written of him (Matthew 26:24). He planned it, wrote it in the Bible, and then carried it out. He established it as truth (Psalm 119:89). Our Memory Verse quotes Him: Search the scriptures . . . they are they which testify of me.
Jesus Fulfilled the Law

Matthew 5:17-18 God gave His righteousness to Israel in the form of the Law. When the Law had served its purpose of showing man his inability to keep it without help, God sent Jesus, His greater Righteousness. Jesus said that He came to fulfill the Law and the Prophets, not destroy them. What they promised, He brought. He was the spiritual fulfillment of the visible, material symbols of the tabernacle worship. For instance, in the place of the blood of goats and calves, which symbolized cleansing from sin, Jesus shed His own blood, which actually cleansed from sin. In place of the ark of the covenant, which symbolized the presence of God, Jesus sent the Holy Spirit to indwell believers. So with all Old Testament types. One jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass . . . till all be fulfilled. The Law, the Old Testament, was not to end and pass out of existence, but to blossom into the New Testament of salvation. Christ Himself made the change from the dispensation of Law to the dispensation of grace that is now in force. So, we see Christ and the Bible are forever joined. Read Psalm 85:7-13.
Jesus' Words Are Spirit and Life

John 6:63 The words that I speak—found in the Bible— they are spirit, and they are life. It is not enough that we know the Bible as literature and history only. Unless we find there the Spirit of God and open our hearts to the Life which is Christ, we have missed it all. Reading the Bible leads us to the living Word, Jesus Christ. But we must believe and obey to have His Spirit and life enter into us and His words abide in us (John 15:7). This is the way we eat His flesh and drink His blood, by which we have eternal life (John 6:54).
JUST A THOUGHT
"He who takes the devil's bait will feel his hook."

In 2 Kings 17:13, we read that the Lord testified against Israel, or gave them no excuse, by all the prophets . . . saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments . . . according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
The Prophets gave warnings, promises, teachings, commands, guidance, and foretelling of events.
But now in these last days— the last dispensation of time—God has spoken unto us by his Son—Jesus Christ.

paragraphs.text: The Bible opens with the account of Creation, and the Hebrew word for God in Genesis 1:1 is plural (Gods). Jesus, together with His Father and the Spirit, created all things (Colossians 1:16). By whom also he made the worlds (Hebrews 1:2). He is the One promised to bruise the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15) and to bless the world through Abraham (Genesis 12:3). He is the Prophet promised to Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15). He is pictured as the Passover Lamb (Exodus 12). He is typified in Isaac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua, David, and others. The Psalms have many prophetic references to Jesus. For example, Psalm 96. The Books of Prophecy promise His coming—Behold, the Lord God will come . . . He shall feed his flock like a shepherd (Isaiah 40:10-11).

paragraphs.text: Luke 24:44 After His Resurrection, Jesus explained His death to His troubled disciples. paragraphs.text: Matthew 5:17-18 God gave His righteousness to Israel in the form of the Law. When the Law had served its purpose of showing man his inability to keep it without help, God sent Jesus, His greater Righteousness. Jesus said that He came to fulfill the Law and the Prophets, not destroy them. What they promised, He brought. He was the spiritual fulfillment of the visible, material symbols of the tabernacle worship. For instance, in the place of the blood of goats and calves, which symbolized cleansing from sin, Jesus shed His own blood, which actually cleansed from sin. In place of the ark of the covenant, which symbolized the presence of God, Jesus sent the Holy Spirit to indwell believers. So with all Old Testament types. One jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass . . . till all be fulfilled. The Law, the Old Testament, was not to end and pass out of existence, but to blossom into the New Testament of salvation. Christ Himself made the change from the dispensation of Law to the dispensation of grace that is now in force. So, we see Christ and the Bible are forever joined. Read Psalm 85:7-13.

paragraphs.text: John 6:63 The words that I speak—found in the Bible— they are spirit, and they are life. It is not enough that we know the Bible as literature and history only. Unless we find there the Spirit of God and open our hearts to the Life which is Christ, we have missed it all. Reading the Bible leads us to the living Word, Jesus Christ. blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 9
THE PURPOSE OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Psalm 102:12-28; Romans 1:14; Romans 16:25-26
Law, history, wisdom, drama, guidance—these are some things the Bible brings to mankind. We have learned that the Prophet was sometimes a foreteller, but more often a forthright preacher.

From the very beginning, there has been a deep yearning for God in the heart of man. God has placed within His written Word, the Bible, direction for man, which, if followed, will lead him from his self-centered life to a soul-satisfying, God-centered life in Christ. Heart highways that lead to Zion! Roads over which God can march into the strongholds of our hearts. The Bible brings down into our daily walk the God Who made the earth and stars and Who keeps the planets in their orbits. He Who in the beginning said, "Let there be light," also speaks the same Word to the darkness of our lives. Jesus, Who wept at the grave of Lazarus, enters into our sorrows still.
MEMORY VERSE: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.—Psalm 119:9
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 4:1-9 Passing on God's Word as it is.
Tue.—Nehemiah 8 Ezra reads God's Law to the people.
Wed.—Luke 8:4-15 Sowing the seed.
Thu.—Romans 1:7-16 Paul's urge to spread the Gospel.
Fri.—Psalm 119:145-160 Pleading God's favor as to His Word.
Devotional Reading: 2 Corinthians 5:14-21 Ministry of reconciliation.
Good News to All People

Psalm 102 This chapter begins with a great cry of distress. In Psalm 102:12 the writer turns to consider God, and hope mounts. He begins to prophesy as God speaks through him of the coming of Christ. He shall appear (Psalm 102:16) bringing salvation to loose those that are appointed to death (Psalm 102:20). He sets his own weakness and shortness of life beside God's strength and endlessness, then shows God's people so closely unified with God as to partake of His eternity (Psalm 102:27-28).

Psalm 102:18-22 This shall be written for the generation to come. God revealed that this good news was to be passed on by the written word. Future generations would read and praise the Lord. Why? Because the Lord would look down from his sanctuary; from heaven, see the needy earth, and hear the groaning of the prisoner—prisoners of Satan bound by the prison bars of sin. Why would He look? To loose those that are appointed to death—to save them from hell. This is the Gospel written beforehand, a picture of the love of God for lost sinners. It was to be delivered to mankind without change to reconcile man and God (2 Corinthians 5:18-19). It was to be proclaimed from Zion and Jerusalem (Micah 4:2; Luke 24:47). Zion, near Jerusalem, was the city of David the king (1 Chronicles 11:5) and was a type of the church (Isaiah 35:10). People and kingdoms would be gathered together . . . to serve the Lord. People cannot be pulled or driven together. They must flow together (Isaiah 2:2). The Prophet here foretells the establishing of God's church, the mountain of the Lord's house. It shall be exalted above the hills. Centuries later, Christ was to liken His disciples to a city that is set on a hill which cannot be hid (Matthew 5:14). And all nations shall flow unto it. Metal cannot be pulled or forced together. The cold, hard hearts of men from all nations, both Jews and Gentiles, are made into one people by the heat of the Holy Spirit melting their hearts together into one people through salvation.

Micah had no faith in any remedy except God. His message was that when men turn to God, they will have peace; when they give up oppression, they will have prosperity. It has always been man's belief that he can

manage his own affairs without any reference to the will and purpose of God. God knew there was no solution for a spiritual problem except the spiritual solution. Never underestimate the importance of the Bible and the power of its Words in the lives of mankind.

All of this must be written in God's Book, the Bible, and passed on to the people of all generations. They are of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation (Revelation 5:9). To reach them, the Bible must be passed on unchanged.
We Owe the Gospel to All People

Romans 1:14 Paul said, I am debtor to Greeks . . . Barbarians . . . wise . . . unwise. What did he owe them? The Gospel (Romans 1:15). Why? Because he had been given it. It was not for him alone—nor for us alone. It was to all people that Jesus came (Luke 2:10). The good tidings of salvation through the Gospel must be shared. To share it, we must have it. Jesus will someday come as a Judge, but He came first as a Savior, and we are living in that day of grace when we may accept him as such. This acceptance should not give us a long face. The happiest people are Christians.
The Gospel Opened to All

Romans 16:25-26 The preaching of Jesus Christ was the revelation of the mystery of God's plan to save sinners. His plan was a mystery because it was kept secret since the world began. When Christ came, it was made manifest, revealed. It was made known to all nations . . . by the scriptures of the prophets. These Old Testament Scriptures foretelling salvation in Christ were preached by the Apostles (Acts 13:14-41). It was by the commandment of the everlasting God that the Gospel was opened to all nations. It remains for His servants to carry it to them. Jesus gave this command just before leaving this world (Matthew 28:19-20; Acts 1:8). We cannot teach Christ unless we have Him. No unsaved person can teach the way to God.
JUST A THOUGHT
Knowledge is one thing that does not become secondhand when used.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 10
THE BIBLE IS INSPIRED
Scripture Texts: Galatians 1:11-12; 2 Timothy 3:15-17; 2 Peter 1:20-21

What is meant by inspiration? The word means "a breathing in." God's breath, or His life, is upon the Words of the Bible. We may read the Bible, but unless we are inspired by the Holy Spirit, it will be only empty words without spiritual life. The breath of the Almighty is on it and in it. It is an authority of truth higher than the authority of the mind.

In 2 Timothy, the Bible lays claim to divine inspiration. Every believing man or woman who has taken this statement at its face value has been brought into a rich, firm experience in spiritual growth.
MEMORY VERSE: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:—2 Timothy 3:16
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—2 Samuel 23:1-7 David claimed inspiration.
Tue.—Galatians 1:1-17 Paul taught the inspired Gospel.
Wed.—Galatians 2:1-9 Apostles recognized Paul's inspiration.
Thu.—1 Peter 1:1-12 The Spirit of Christ inspired prophecy.
Fri.—Psalm 119:97-112 David’s love for God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 3:1-12 Paul taught by the Spirit.
Paul's Claim to Inspiration

Galatians 1:11-12 I certify—what Paul is about to say is sure and certain. The gospel which was preached of me is not after man—not of man's thinking. Neither was I taught it— not learned from human teachers— but by the revelation of Jesus Christ—it was revealed to him by Jesus. Paul's knowledge in the mystery of Christ was received by revelation (Ephesians 3:2-5). Jesus promised this when He appeared to Paul on the road to Damascus (Acts 26:16).

A small part of the Bible—the Ten Commandments—God Himself wrote (Exodus 31:18; Exodus 32:16). Other parts, He spoke (Exodus 25:1; Jeremiah 30:2; Revelation 2:1). Still other parts were written as the Holy Spirit took control of the thoughts of a man (Ephesians 1:17-18).

Inspiration is not revelation, but revelation is inspiration. Revelation is that act of God by which He directly communicates truth not known before. Examples of revealed truth are 1 Corinthians 15 and 1 Thessalonians 4, the future resurrection; 1 Timothy 4:1-3, the coming apostasy; and the visions in the Book of Revelation. Not all Scripture needed to be revealed. Some was already known. But all, both the revealed and the known, were inspired. Inspiration is the guidance of the Holy Spirit in telling or writing of truth already revealed (Job 32:8).

The Bible records both sins and right acts, sayings of Satan and sayings of God. Not all were inspired when done or said. But the RECORD of them is inspired and true. The Holy Spirit selected the writer and the matter to be written and directed in the writing.
All Sacred Scripture Inspired

2 Timothy 3:15-17 The Holy Scriptures which Timothy knew are the Old Testament Books. In recommending them, Paul says All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable . . . The writings given to Israel for their guidance and which they gathered together and looked upon as God's Word, are the same as our Old Testament upon which Jesus put His approval. These were called the Scriptures or Holy

Scriptures (John 5:39; Romans 1:2; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4). Because they are inspired by God, they are true and are profitable. For what? Doctrine—for teaching God's will, Jesus Christ, and the way to be saved. Reproof—to warn sinners of the result if they do not repent. Correction—a standard to bring men back to true doctrine and the right way, as they have a tendency to go astray. Instruction in righteousness—to give knowledge of God, His ways, and how to please Him. These are to make the man of God—any who belongs to Him—perfect and thoroughly furnished. Everything is furnished that is needed for a perfect life in Christ. No one is furnished or trained or educated for the good life without knowledge of and belief in the Bible (Proverbs 9:10).

Sometimes the word inspired is mistakenly applied to a song, poem, or writing not in the Bible. There is a difference between a divine revelation of the mind of God and a divine action on the mind of man. The former is revelation; the latter is spiritual enlightenment or inspiration. We hear it said, "I did not see this before. I am going to walk in this light." That truth has been revealed for centuries, but it just became light or truth to you by the Holy Spirit's inspiration. The Bible is God's public revelation; what He says to us in our daily, private worship is for us and for our needs. God speaks to us through the Bible, prayer, worship, and the conscience. Both individuals and nations are enlightened by its use.
The Holy Spirit Gave the Word

2 Peter 1:20-21 No prophecy of the scripture—no God-given message—is of any private interpretation. We must not give it OUR meaning but let the Giver interpret it for us. The prophecy came not . . . by the will of man. We must go to the One with authority. If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God (James 1:5). Holy men of God spake . . . moved by the Holy Ghost. This spoken of the Old Testament is equally true of the New. New Testament preachers preached with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven. They also wrote it (1 Peter 1:12). Two agents here—holy men and the Holy Ghost. He moved them—stirred their desires and guided their thoughts. They wrote as He guided. The Lord gave the word (Psalm 68:11). This is God's way of preserving His Word against destruction.

Those things which we cannot understand, we are asked to accept on faith, and it has been the experience of believers through the ages that when they manifest such faith, the things they could not honestly understand either became clear to them or ceased to be a cause of anxiety and bewilderment.
We must beware of "cunningly devised fables," for such mislead the faithful today when men substitute their own theories for the infallible Word of God.
JUST A THOUGHT
"The principles of the Bible are the groundwork of human freedom."

LESSON 11
THE BIBLE HAS POWER AND AUTHORITY
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 55:11; Luke 16:17; John 15:7; Hebrews 4:12; Acts 20:32

The Bible bears the sovereign authority of God. It is true. It is powerful. The Word of God is living and is active. It is the Book into which the all-powerful, all-knowing, and all-loving God has breathed the breath of spiritual life. When Jesus came, this powerful Word was made flesh, which dwelt among us, full of grace and truth.

The whole world is sinking deeper every day into a lower level of spiritual illiteracy. Only the power and authority of the Bible can lift it to a higher plain. But only as mankind reads and obeys its teachings will it have a leveling effect upon a world that is sinking to tragic destruction.
MEMORY VERSE: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.— Ephesians 6:17
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Jeremiah 23:18-32 — God’s Word versus false prophecies.
Tue.—Matthew 8:5-13 — The power of Christ's Words.
Wed.—Mark 7:1-13 — Human tradition is wrong.
Thu.—John 8:23-32 — Jesus spoke as His Father taught Him.
Fri.—Psalm 119:113-128 — David's hope in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 55 — God's Word shall fulfill His will.
God's Word Has Power to Succeed

Isaiah 55:11 My word . . . shall not return unto me void— not be without result—shall accomplish . . . shall prosper. God put power into His Word. He links His Word with His purpose. I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it (Isaiah 46:11).

Luke 16:17 Jesus expressed the certainty of God's Word to succeed. It is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail. It cannot, for the authority of God is in it. Power comes from authority. God has authority because He is Author of all things, so, greater than they. Read Mark 1:22. Not all who hear the Word will accept it, but some will (Mark 4:14-20). His word was with power (Luke 4:32). Power to do what? To carry out each Word. His power and authority came from God, His Father. Jesus was the Word which became flesh and dwelt among them.
God's Word Gives Power in Prayer

John 15:7 If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you. Here is the power to unite man with God and to bring into our lives all the power which God's Word affords us. For if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us (1 John 5:14). Every promise in the Bible is ours. What unites them? (1) If ye abide in me—in Christ, yielded to Him, dead to self, and alive in Christ (Colossians 3:3; Galatians 2:20). (2) If my words abide in you—if you believe, obey, and love His Words until they are spirit and life in you (John 6:63), until they lead to the living Word, Christ Jesus. The connection being made, God's Word is set in motion to answer the prayer. Power comes from authority. The authority of God is in His Word.
