SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 11
God's Word Has Power to Penetrate Hard Hearts

Hebrews 4:12 The word of God is quick—living. Powerful— can do God's will. Sharper than any two-edged sword—no dull or ineffective edge. It divides between soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow— pairs very nearly alike and hard to separate. They are used figuratively to express the power of the Bible to penetrate. As a living thing, it is a discerner. It puts the finger on the very point where guilt or virtue has its center in the heart. It sees through words to thoughts, past acts to intents. It points them out to us, convicting and directing. For instance, it tells us hatred is murder (1 John 3:15), all sins begin in the heart (Mark 7:21-23), and the Kingdom of God is entered only by spiritual birth (John 3:5).

This sharp, two-edged sword cuts to pieces our selfishness and sin. The Bible says no to many of our cherished plans. It cuts deep into the customs of men. It puts a roadblock in front of fleshly passions. It bids us to be merciful if we would receive mercy.

Praise God when it cuts down into your life, separating those things which tend to hold us back and take away our liberty and freedom. Let the Bible criticize you before your conscience and the world get a chance to do so.
God's Word Has Power to Save

Acts 20:32 I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace—the Bible, which ministers God's grace, or a supply of His life. The Word is able to build you up—to give you knowledge, spiritual strength, faith. And an inheritance among the sanctified—to give possessions which sanctified ones have— life, holiness, power, love, faith, fruit of the Spirit, and a home in Heaven. One does not get these by having a Bible only, or reading it only, or going through forms, or performing outward works. No, only by hearing, believing, and obeying is one led to Christ Who saves (James 1:21-25). We must do the will of the Father (Matthew 7:21). The Bible shows us His will.

In God's Word is the authority of God. For effective work that accomplishes God's will, we must use it. When a child inquires, read with him the answer from the Bible. To lead the unsaved to Christ, use Scripture. People need instructing, the church needs reviving, lives need changing, and problems need solving. There is only one way to do this, and that is to stand in God's counsel and cause the people to hear His Words, seasoned with prayer (Jeremiah 23:22).

All this power is unleashed by faith in God's Word. It is all rendered powerless by unbelief. Enemies of God have always tried to take authority away from His Word, the Bible. Unbelief has taken various forms from the time of Eden until now. Some are: (1) Atheism—denial of the existence of God. (2) Agnosticism— the doctrine that one cannot know as to the nature of God, a future life, etc. (3) Infidelity—lack of faith, unbelief. It denies the truth of the Bible and Christian teachings. (4) Higher Criticism— critical study of the Bible, aimed to find faults within. The writers of the Bible were not its authors; the Holy Spirit was. The writers were put in trust with the gospel (1 Thessalonians 2:3-4).
JUST A THOUGHT
Unbelievers are not convinced by factual evidence, but by the Spirit's power working in a life.

They are used figuratively to express the power of the Bible to penetrate.
As a living thing, it is a discerner.
It puts the finger on the very point where guilt or virtue has its center in the heart.
It sees through words to thoughts, past acts to intents.
It points them out to us, convicting and directing.
For instance, it tells us hatred is murder (1 John 3:15), all sins begin in the heart (Mark 7:21-23), and the Kingdom of God is entered only by spiritual birth (John 3:5).
This sharp, two-edged sword cuts to pieces our selfishness and sin.
The Bible says no to many of our cherished plans.
It cuts deep into the customs of men.
It puts a roadblock in front of fleshly passions.
It bids us to be merciful if we would receive mercy.
Praise God when it cuts down into your life, separating those things which tend to hold us back and take away our liberty and freedom.
Let the Bible criticize you before your conscience and the world get a chance to do so.

The Word is able to build you up—to give you knowledge, spiritual strength, faith.
And an inheritance among the sanctified—to give possessions which sanctified ones have— life, holiness, power, love, faith, fruit of the Spirit, and a home in Heaven.

No, only by hearing, believing, and obeying is one led to Christ Who saves (James 1:21-25).
We must do the will of the Father (Matthew 7:21).
The Bible shows us His will.
In God's Word is the authority of God.
For effective work that accomplishes God's will, we must use it.
When a child inquires, read with him the answer from the Bible.
To lead the unsaved to Christ, use Scripture.
People need instructing, the church needs reviving, lives need changing, and problems need solving.
There is only one way to do this, and that is to stand in God's counsel and cause the people to hear His Words, seasoned with prayer (Jeremiah 23:22).
All this power is unleashed by faith in God's Word.
It is all rendered powerless by unbelief.
Enemies of God have always tried to take authority away from His Word, the Bible.
Unbelief has taken various forms from the time of Eden until now.
Some are: (1) Atheism—denial of the existence of God. (2) Agnosticism— the doctrine that one cannot know as to the nature of God, a future life, etc. (3) Infidelity—lack of faith, unbelief.
It denies the truth of the Bible and Christian teachings. (4) Higher Criticism— critical study of the Bible, aimed to find faults within.
The writers of the Bible were not its authors; the Holy Spirit was.
The writers were put in trust with the gospel (1 Thessalonians 2:3-4).
Unbelievers are not convinced by factual evidence, but by the Spirit's power working in a life.

lessons.title: THE BIBLE HAS POWER AND AUTHORITY

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 12
OUR USE OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: 1Peter 2:2-3; Hebrews 5:12-14; Deuteronomy 6:6-7; Luke 11:28; 2 Timothy 3:16-17

It is not enough to own a Bible. We must hunger for it, hunger to read it, take it into our hearts. We cannot be hungry by trying. Start in and read it. That helps. But the only way to complete your desire is told in 1 Peter 2:2-3—if you are saved. The taste of Jesus brings hunger for His Word. As we hunger and read, the Holy Spirit brings a greater understanding. When we read it with the God-given desire, we will grow thereby.

Since God gave us the Bible to use, it is our responsibility to use it. We must believe it, take it without addition or subtraction, obey it, teach it to our children, and spread its message to all people. For us to use the Bible, we must know it. If we do not use it correctly, we will lose it directly. Use it rightfully, and it is effective.
MEMORY VERSE: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.—Luke 11:28
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 6:1-7 Teaching the Word at home.
Tue.—Amos 8:4-14 A famine of the Word.
Wed.—Hebrews 5:12-14 Progress from milk to meat.
Thu.—1 Peter 2:1-8 Only the saved grow by the Word.
Fri.—Psalm 119:161-176 The preciousness of God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Matthew 7:21-29 The wise obey God's Word.
Hunger for the Word

1 Peter 2:2-3 As newborn babes, desire . . . These are people who had been born again, quickened, or made alive, by the Word. Being made alive by the Word, they need the Word to continue in this new life. As the newborn infant requires milk for nourishment, so the newborn Christian needs the sincere milk of the word to live thereby. As the natural baby's first desire is to find something to eat, so the newborn Christian will desire the Word of God. However, we cannot desire of ourselves, and God does not ask us to. He plants the desire when He saves and fills us with the Spirit. We cultivate the desire. He satisfies as we obey. The sincere milk— the pure, unadulterated, plain teachings of God which are found in the Bible. That ye may grow . . . Milk makes a baby grow. God's Word makes a soul grow wiser, stronger, more godly, more effectual in prayer, and more able to be of service to God. If so be—a condition attached— that ye have tasted—experienced the saving grace of the Lord, been born again. A baby must live before it can eat and grow. A soul must live spiritually before it can eat and grow by the Word. A natural, or unsaved, one might read the Bible for years and never grow (1 Corinthians 2:14). The order is: live, eat, grow.
Study the Word

Hebrews 5:12 Ye ought to be teachers. These Hebrews had heard the Gospel so many years and professed to be followers of the Lord. They should know the truth and be capable of teaching it to others, but were still children in understanding, unable to understand the deeper truths (meats). They still required milk (the primary principles of the Word). Some people are ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth (2 Timothy 3:7). They hear the Gospel, but not mixed with faith in them, it is to no avail. Read Romans 2:13; James 1:21-25. Under the same preaching, some will grow spiritually, while others die (1 Corinthians 10:3-5).
© 2015 Church of God, Inc. Our Use of the Bible ─ Lesson 12 www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 12

Hebrews 5:13 He is a babe—He who understands only the primary doctrines of the Gospel testifies that he is only a babe (beginner) in Christ. Perhaps he has failed to study the Word and apply it to his life, or is dull of hearing (Hebrews 5:11; Acts 28:27). We should diligently study God's Word and come to a mature understanding of the deeper truths and not tarry with the primary doctrines such as repentance and faith.

Hebrews 5:14 Strong meat—The deeper, richer truths of God belong to the older saint rather than the newborn because he has grown and matured. A baby cannot be expected to digest the same food as an older person, neither should he be a baby forever. Those who by reason of use have their senses exercised— Those who have searched its pages with a hungry and believing heart, have obeyed its commands, have grown to be stalwart Christians, able to discern good from evil. Parents become concerned when a baby lacks growth and proper development in due time. So should it cause concern when a babe in Christ fails to develop into more than a spiritual bottle baby. Healthy babies grow up. Many have been deceived by some smooth-tongued, would-be prophet because they failed to study the Word and so were unable to discern truth from error. Every saint, whatever his place in the church, should be a teacher of the Bible.
Teach the Word in the Home

Deuteronomy 6:6-7 In thine heart—The Christian should prize the Word of God above all else. Like David, we should hide it in our hearts (Psalm 119:11). If it be not in our hearts, it will profit us nothing. Thou shalt teach . . . thy children. God commands Israel to teach His Word to their offspring. Christians should consider the Bible the supreme Book of the home. Along with some other good books are many bad books. They can influence and mislead, thus wrecking one's Christian life. With all diligence, patience, and understanding, we should teach the Word to our children while they are young, that it may mold their lives as they grow. The Word never returns empty (Isaiah 55:11). If received into the heart, it will save; if rejected, it will damn.
Obey the Word

Luke 11:28 Jesus said, Yea rather, blessed are they— Some are more blessed than others. Blessed is the mother who bore Jesus (Luke 11:27). More blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. This is how much God values obedience. Not everyone that saith . . . but he that doeth the will of my Father . . . The wise man whose house will not fall is whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them (Matthew 7:21, Matthew 7:24). To fall short in obedience is to lose all.
Be Equipped With the Word

2 Timothy 3:16-17 All scripture . . . is profitable . . . throughly furnished . . . The end result of eating food is strength to do. So, the end result of taking the Word of God is spiritual strength to do all good works. Thus we are equipped to fill our place in the church. First, we must take His Word into our souls; then we can give it out to others. No taking in, no giving out effectively.
Hands Off the Word

Revelation 22:18-19 If every commandment is observed fully, it will accomplish its purpose. I testify— Jesus speaking—If any man shall add . . . God shall add . . . plagues . . . If any man take away . . . God shall take away his part . . . It is a dangerous thing to tamper with the Bible. We are not to add to nor subtract from it. To add to its precepts is to suffer the judgments of God; to diminish from it is to lose the blessings it offers. We must handle the Bible with fear and reverence.

units.text: 1 Peter 2:2-3 As newborn babes, desire . . .
These are people who had been born again, quickened, or made alive, by the Word.
Being made alive by the Word, they need the Word to continue in this new life.
As the newborn infant requires milk for nourishment, so the newborn Christian needs the sincere milk of the word to live thereby.
As the natural baby's first desire is to find something to eat, so the newborn Christian will desire the Word of God.
However, we cannot desire of ourselves, and God does not ask us to.
He plants the desire when He saves and fills us with the Spirit.
We cultivate the desire.
He satisfies as we obey.
The sincere milk— the pure, unadulterated, plain teachings of God which are found in the Bible.
That ye may grow . . .
Milk makes a baby grow.
God's Word makes a soul grow wiser, stronger, more godly, more effectual in prayer, and more able to be of service to God.
If so be—a condition attached— that ye have tasted—experienced the saving grace of the Lord, been born again.
A baby must live before it can eat and grow.
A soul must live spiritually before it can eat and grow by the Word.
A natural, or unsaved, one might read the Bible for years and never grow (1 Corinthians 2:14).
The order is: live, eat, grow.

paragraphs.text: Hebrews 5:12 Ye ought to be teachers. These Hebrews had heard the Gospel so many years and professed to be followers of the Lord. They should know the truth and be capable of teaching it to others, but were still children in understanding, unable to understand the deeper truths (meats). They still required milk (the primary principles of the Word). Some people are ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth (2 Timothy 3:7). They hear the Gospel, but not mixed with faith in them, it is to no avail. Read Romans 2:13; James 1:21-25. Under the same preaching, some will grow spiritually, while others die (1 Corinthians 10:3-5).

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 13
THE BIBLE AT THE JUDGMENT
Scripture Texts: John 12:47-50; Romans 2:11-16; Revelation 20:12-15
We are all to be judged according to how our lives measure up to the Bible and our attitude toward obeying its commandments.

Is there a more solemn thought than that we must stand and be judged by God? He has told us the standard by which we will be judged. He has written it in a Book and given us the Book. He has given the Holy Spirit to teach us His Word and enlighten all that are born into the world. What is the wise course for us to take? Why do some not take it? Saints have an obligation to acquaint others with the Bible.
MEMORY VERSE: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.—John 12:48
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ezekiel 13:1-14 False prophets to be punished.
Tue.—Mark 8:34-38 Must not be ashamed of Christ's Words.
Wed.—Romans 2:1-16 To be judged according to knowledge.
Thu.—1 Peter 3:9-18 Being ready for the Lord.
Fri.—Psalm 119:129-144 David's great longing for God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Revelation 22:12-21 Danger in changing God's Word.
Christ's Words Will Judge Us

John 12:47-48 I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. (See John 3:17.) Jesus came in love for mankind. His foremost desire was to save sinners and bring them to Himself. He desired to make us a holy family together here in this life, so we could be together in the next. But He cannot let down His holy standard. His Word is changeless. He could not save if it were not. So if one rejects Him by receiving not His Words, he puts himself under the condemnation of those Words. The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day—the Day of Judgment, which is to come when all are resurrected as told in John 5:28-30. The Words of God spoken to us now are a preliminary judgment of that which will be final then. If we cannot pass the test as Christ's Word checks us out here, we can never hope to pass at the final Judgment. In the preliminary, we have an opportunity to change it, but at the final Judgment, we have no chance of change.
Authority Behind Christ's Words

John 12:49-50 I have not spoken of myself. None of the Trinity speaks or works alone. They have perfect unity. The Father . . . gave me a commandment . . . what I should speak. The authority of the Father is in ALL the Words of Jesus—for whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak. Jesus said, He that hath the Son hath life—to have His Word is to have Christ. God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son (1 John 5:11-12). His salvation is a system of eternal life to bring the power of God to dying, miserable man. It will not do man any good that he has believed that Christ has come in the flesh to destroy the works of the devil if he does not come unto Him and receive life, but continues to live under the power and guilt of sin.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 13
Judged According to the Gospel

Romans 2:11-15 As many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law—will perish, not being born again. But their punishment will be less severe than of those who knew God's will and His offer of salvation (Luke 12:47-48). Romans 2:14-15 tell us that the Gentiles—heathens—all have a law written in their hearts, their conscience. This is the law these ones will be judged by. As many as have sinned in the law—Moses' Law, knowing the law—shall be judged by the law— must measure to the requirements they knew or be punished accordingly.

Romans 2:16 God shall judge the secrets of men. The inmost heart will be laid bare (Luke 12:2). By Jesus Christ—He will be our Judge then, no more our Mediator (2 Corinthians 5:10). According to my gospel—the Gospel Paul preached, the Gospel of Christ. The Gospel is the standard of judgment. Have you received it? Have you loved to obey it? (1 John 5:3).

If those ignorant of God's Word will be beaten with few stripes (Luke 12:48), might it be better not to know? But one without the Word and so, without Christ, must perish. Though his stripes be fewer, still they are stripes. He is forever cut off from Christ and eternal life. It is best to know and to obey God's Word. Can one plead ignorance by closing the Bible and refusing to read? No. To know where to find God's Word or even that He gave a Word, is enough knowledge to make one accountable for knowing and obeying.
God's Books Will Measure Our Works

Revelation 20:12-15 And I saw the dead small, and great, stand before God . . . This is the final Judgment of all people, the only Judgment the Bible tells of. . . . they were judged every man according to their works. Two kinds of books are opened: (1) the books and (2) the book of life. The books are the standard of measurement by which each is to be judged, for the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books. And also, according to their works. Our works—the thoughts, words, and deeds of our lives—will be held beside the commands in the Books. They must agree. Their quality must measure to the quality required. If so, we will pass the Judgment. If not, we will be lost forever—a great tragedy! These Books are those which contain the Word Christ has spoken and the Gospel, the Bible. The other Book, the book of life, lists the names of God's children, those who will pass the Judgment and enter Heaven. Our names must be written in the book of life while we are in this world—before we die. It is written there when we are made alive in Christ—saved, born again (Luke 10:20). Can you remember when your name was written in the pages of the book of life?
JUST A THOUGHT
What are you doing with the Bible?

Can you remember when your name was written in the pages of the book of life?

lines.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
THE BIBLE, GOD'S WORD
Scripture Texts: Psalm 19:7-11; Psalm 119:89
The Bible used to have a larger place in the life of our people than now.
It was read in many homes, used as an early school reader, studied,
believed, and reverenced. Government leaders looked to it for foundation
principles. Much literature contained Bible quotations. The Bible was read
in schools, and passages from it were in reading books.
Gradually the Bible has been neglected. Fewer and fewer homes have
family worship. Schools have dropped its use. As more Bibles lay closed,
more people grow up ignorant of its teachings and indifferent to its
authority. As a result, our nation has sunk to its lowest spiritual state. The Bible has the answer to every question
and the solution to every problem that man faces today. God's Word is perfect in every way. It is genuine,
authentic, and authoritative.
MEMORY VERSE: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand forever.
—Isaiah 40:8
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 4:2-14 As the Lord commanded.
Tues.—Isaiah 59:16-21 God's Word is forever.
Wed.—Jeremiah 36 Punished for burning God's Word.
Thurs.—Ezekiel 33:21-29 God inspired Ezekiel.
Fri.—2 Thessalonians 2:1-13 Not man's word, but God's.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 19 God speaks to man.
Description of God's Word
Psalm 19:7-9 Five different names are given here by David to God's Word—law . . . testimony . . . statutes
. . . commandment . . . judgments. Each adds a little different shade of meaning. He tells us it is perfect . . .
sure . . . right . . . pure . . . clean . . . true . . . righteous altogether. It is sure—solid, strong, dependable. It is
pure—unmixed. It is righteous altogether—no wrong or foreign bits in it. There are unbelievers who say the
Bible merely "contains" the Word of God (along with many human words). No, it is the unmixed Word of God.
It is right and good because God is good.
What God's Word Does
The Word of God blesses the whole man. Converting the soul—bringing salvation to it. Making wise—
educates the mind. Rejoicing the heart—believing and obeying brings greatest joy. Enlightening the eyes—a
Spirit-filled saint has a brighter look at life. Enduring forever—the saint who keeps the Word of God in the
fear of the Lord will endure forever, living a strong and effective life.
Psalm 19:10-11 The wise, Spirit-filled one desires the Word of God. He has a real hunger and thirst for the
Bible. He feels a need for it in his life each day. It is more precious than gold and sweeter also than honey.
Gold speaks of value, honey of enjoyment. The Bible warns—shows the danger of straying from the right. In
keeping of them—obedience—there is great reward, both here and in Heaven.
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
The Bible, God’s Word─Lesson 1
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
A Settled Word
Psalm 119:89 Forever—eternally past, present, and future—God's word is settled in heaven. It is sure and
changeless. Man cannot reach there to set it aside. He may reject or disobey it, but he cannot change it. The
Word of God will change man, but man cannot change the Word of God. Read what happened to a man who
burned God's Word in Jeremiah, Chapter 36.
Reason for the Bible
It is just natural that an all-wise Creator would communicate with His Creation. Would He make a world as
complex as this, with many forms of life as well as the human mind and spirit, then abandon it without care or
control? That would be unthinkable. He gave His Word to man in the Bible. It is a compass and chart to guide
him along on his journey in this world.
The Bible, from beginning to end, recognizes that there is a definite and known Word of God. It shows itself
to be that Word. Hundreds of times we read the word of the Lord came . . . God said . . . the commandments
of God . . . thus saith the Lord, etc. It simply states this with no attempt to prove it, which is a characteristic of
truth.
God reveals Himself to man through (1) nature, (2) the Bible, (3) Jesus, and (4) the Holy Spirit. The Bible is
the path by which we are led to Christ and the Spirit.
The Bible is a collection of sixty-six Books, written by a number of authors, over about sixteen hundred
years. The chief theme running throughout the Bible is the reclaiming of man from sin to eternal fellowship with
God.
The Bible has two divisions—the Old Testament with thirty-nine Books and the New Testament with
twenty-seven Books. The Old Testament tells of man's fall into sin and God's promise of salvation from it. It
tells of God's choosing of a people for Himself through whom to send the Savior. To them, He gave the Law in
preparation for salvation. The New Testament begins with the coming of the Savior and unfolds the plan of
salvation to its culmination in Heaven. It tells of the gathering of a people of God—the church—to enjoy this
salvation. The two Testaments are closely related. Almost all of the Old Testament was written in the Hebrew
language. The New Testament was written in Greek. For people of other languages to read the Bible, it had to be
translated into their languages. Any certain translation is called a version.
A Great Loss
All over the land are various moves for or against the Bible. When people lose the Bible, they open the door
to all kinds of evil and invite God's judgments. We are losing the Bible in many cases. We must do all we can to
bring it back. How can we do this? By using it and preserving it in our own individual lives. Put it back into our
homes and lives. We may have to die for it yet. But isn't the Bible worth the cost? Many in times past considered
it so.
This quarter's lessons accent the Bible with the purpose of increasing our knowledge of, love for, and
obedience to, the Bible. But the Sunday school will never be enough to stem the tide of evil rolling across the
land. Daily, personal home worship is necessary. Without it, we are saying by our example, "The Bible is not
important." With it and obedience to it, we can arm ourselves with the strength of God. God grant that we do so.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is harder to crush a half-truth than a whole lie.

LESSON 2
WHAT THE OLD TESTAMENT IS
Scripture Texts: Romans 15:4; 2 Peter 1:19-21; 1 Corinthians 10:11;
Exodus 19:5-6; Ezekiel 18:4; Isaiah 55:7
The history of the Bible is interpreted from the religious standpoint.
Although the Prophets predicted certain events in the future, they were
particularly preachers of righteousness and disclosers of God's purpose.
From beginning to end, the Bible shows itself to be God's Book, our spiritual
guide. The only thing greater than the Word of God is the Word made flesh.
The whole testimony of the Bible points toward the coming of Jesus and
fulfilling of His saving ministry among men.
The Bible is supernatural in nature. It is God's message to His children.
The Old Testament is for our example and teaching. It tells of the curse of
sin, the promise of a Redeemer, and the choosing of a people for His name. The Old Testament is thirty-nine
Books, divided into five groups.
MEMORY VERSE: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as
they were moved by the Holy Ghost. —2 Peter 1:21
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Exodus 12:1-14, 40-51 The Lord delivers Israel.
Tue.—Nehemiah 2:1-9 Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem.
Wed.—Psalm 16 A song of trust and praise.
Thu.—Isaiah 53 The atonement of Christ foretold.
Fri.—Joel 2:12-32 Promise of forgiveness and the Spirit.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 119:1-16 Blessing of Word on a life.
Purpose of the Old Testament
Romans 15:4 In the preceding verse Paul speaks of Christ and His voluntary taking of suffering upon
Himself for others. He applies Psalm 69:9 to Christ. Then—whatsoever things were written aforetime—
former writings, or the Old Testament—all were written for our learning. These Scriptures are for us. They
are not out-of-date, useless books. Learn from them. Feed on the patience and comfort found there. Believe the
promises. Hope in them.
2 Peter 1:19-21 The prophecy—the message from God—in old time. This is the Old Testament. It came
not . . . by the will of man—was not human thought. It originated with God. The Holy Ghost . . . moved . . .
holy men of God to speak or to write these words. The Old Testament came from God that it might be as a lamp
shining in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts.
1 Corinthians 10:11 All these things—incidents of the journey of Israel to Canaan—happened . . . for
ensamples to us. Us upon whom the ends of the world are come— the last dispensation before the end of
time. The Old Testament is for us. Study it, not to observe the forms of the Law, but to learn God's way.
It Tells of a People of God
Exodus 19:5-6 Ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me . . . a kingdom of priests . . . an holy nation.
This, God spoke to old Israel. But there were terms to be met if they were to be this people. If ye will obey my
voice indeed, and keep my covenant. Upon these same terms, we now can be God's special, peculiar people,
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
What The Old Testament Is—Lesson 2
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
His church (1 Peter 2:4-10). Only we have a different covenant now, not to keep the Law, but to repent and
believe on Jesus Christ.
It Tells of God's Forgiveness
Ezekiel 18:4 The soul that sinneth, it shall die. This is the unchanging Law of God. When Adam sinned,
he let death into the world, death to both soul and body. The only escape is through Jesus Christ (John 1:29).
Isaiah 55:7 Escape from sin is by way of repentance—Let the wicked forsake his way—turn to Christ—
return unto the Lord—gain the forgiveness of God—He will have mercy . . . he will abundantly pardon.
This is God's wonderful plan of salvation always existing in His purpose, promised and begun in the Old
Testament, fulfilled in the New. His plan is always the same in principle. Only the outward forms of it differ
under different covenants.
The Old Testament begins a continuous story of the Bible. It is of a contest between Satan and God for
possession of man whom God created. Ancient Bibles were written by hand on parchment of goatskins or
sheepskins, and then rolled into scrolls. Our Old Testament is thirty-nine Books, divided into five groups. The
Jews had the same material but combined them in different order, and in three divisions: the Law, the Prophets,
and the Holy Writings or Psalms (Luke 24:44). We have glimpsed a few leading points in the Old Testament.
Let us now look at the Books.
The Five Books of the Law
Genesis opens with the account of Creation. God looked at what He had made and found it very good. But
the devil came and tempted man to sin and thus brought spiritual and physical death to all mankind. Sin
increased until God punished by destroying mankind with a flood, saving only Noah and his family. Man's pride
led him to plan the city and Tower of Babel. God again punished by confusing the language and scattering the
people. Now God began to build a nation through whom to send a Savior and to give His Word to man. The
Israelites became slaves in Egypt, a type of sin's bondage.
Exodus tells of God's miraculous deliverance from that slavery and the giving of the Law. He delivered by
means of the ten plagues. At Mt. Sinai God gave the Law (writing with His own finger), and the tabernacle was
built to God's specifications. All the provisions of God for Israel were types of God's later provisions for the
church.
Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy continues recounting the Law and the journey to Canaan, Israel's
homeland. The Law required holiness. It forbade making or serving idols. It taught there is but one God, the
Supreme and living One. The Law made provision for animal blood sacrifices for atonement for sin, pointing
forward in type to the perfect sacrifice of the blood of Christ.
The Books of History
These continue the history of Israel after Moses' death. Joshua led them into Canaan and governed until his
death, being followed by Judges and Kings. It is a sad story of Israel's sins and of God's love and wrath. The
nation became split into Judah and Israel. Finally, God allowed Judah to be overcome and carried away captive
to Babylon. The Books of Ezra and Nehemiah are accounts of the return of some of the Jews to Jerusalem and
the rebuilding of the temple.
Books of Poetry
Job teaches trust in God through affliction and discouragement. The Psalms are songs of praise and
worship. The Proverbs are wise sayings of Solomon, teaching obedience to God. Ecclesiastes is a look at life to
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
What The Old Testament Is—Lesson 2
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
discover the ultimate good. The Song of Solomon is a beautiful song of the love of a man and a maiden. It is a
type of the love of Christ and the church for each other.
Books of Prophecy
Both Major and Minor Prophets were written by Prophets, men who spoke to men for God. These messages
from God are warnings and judgment upon certain groups, encouragement, comfort, instruction, and predictions.
These predictions rise to their greatest height in foretelling the coming of Christ. We must look to the New
Testament for the fulfillment of this.
Although the Old Testament has so much sin to tell, still scattered through every age were great men who
obeyed God, such as Enoch, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Samuel, David, Daniel, Elijah, Elisha, and Jeremiah. The
Law was given to show man his inability to keep it in his own strength and his need of a Savior.
JUST A THOUGHT
You will never know the Bible until you know its Author.

What The Old Testament Is—Lesson 2
www.GodsAcres.org

LESSON 3
HOW THE OLD TESTAMENT CAME TO US
Scripture Text: Psalm 145:1-13
God began to give His Word to man by speaking to him. He spoke to man
in all ages, giving personal commands. When ready to give a system of law
for guidance over a length of time, He first spoke it (Exodus 20:1-19), then
He wrote part of it with His own finger (Exodus 31:18), then commanded
Moses to write thou these words (Exodus 24:4; 34:27), and Moses obeyed.
All Old Testament Books were written as God led the writers to write
(Jeremiah 30:2; Habakkuk 2:2; 2 Peter 1:21). With few exceptions, they
were written in Hebrew on parchment and rolled into scrolls to make a book. These were copied by hand by
scribes, an expensive and laborious task.
The Old Testament is God's Word, was written to stand forever, and is to be spread to all people.
MEMORY VERSE: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the
mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.—Isaiah 40:5
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—2 Kings 22 Hilkiah finds a Bible.
Tue.—2 Kings 23:1-25 Josiah obeys the Bible.
Wed.—Isaiah 40:1-11 God's Word and promise will stand.
Thu.—Isaiah 45:17-23 Message of salvation for all people.
Fri.—Psalm 119:17-32 Prayer for the blessing of God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 62 Whole world to know of salvation.
Praise Passed Along
Psalm 145:1-9 In this song of praise and adoration of the Lord, David expresses the desire of his heart that
all people should know God and join in praising Him. This is God's will. (Read Numbers 14:21.) One
generation shall praise thy works to another—each generation has a responsibility to pass the good news on
and on to others. Men shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts . . . they shall abundantly utter the
memory of thy great goodness. How will they know these? Because the record—God's Word—has been
passed on to them. (Read Isaiah 40:1-8.) David had only the part of the Old Testament which was written to
that date.
How Will They Know?
Psalm 145:10-12 Thy saints shall bless thee. They shall speak . . . and talk. The saints can never keep the
mighty works of the Lord to themselves, for of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh (Luke 6:45).
Of what shall they speak? The glory of thy kingdom . . . thy power. Why? To make known to the sons of
men—other people—his mighty acts— God's acts of power, of love and mercy. And the glorious majesty of
his kingdom—salvation, His work in the hearts of men, His spiritual rule in the earth, the glory of His divine
organism, the church, which unites men and God. The saints are to speak, to proclaim this to the world. To do
this, they must have and pass on the Bible.
God's Will
Psalm 145:13 We see from this Psalm that God's will is that His Word, His message, be given to all men of
every generation. His is an everlasting kingdom. See Isaiah 9:6-7. Therefore, His Word by which He rules
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
How The Old Testament Came To Us─Lesson3
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
must reach to all generations. He has provided for its preservation. It has come to us because God willed it so,
and certain people did His will.
God directed scribes to write by hand the Books of the Law. Some were Ezra, Baruch, and others (Ezra 7:6;
Jeremiah 36:4). The book of the law was to be kept in the ark of the covenant of the Lord (Deuteronomy
31:26). The Books were to be read to the people (Joshua 8:34-35; Deuteronomy 31:9-13). This custom
continued through the time of Christ and of Paul, reading weekly in the synagogue (Luke 4:16-17; Acts 13:14-
15). God's Word was to be taught to the children (Deuteronomy 4:9; Deuteronomy 6:6-7, Deuteronomy 6:20-
25). Kings were to have God's Book and to live and rule by it (Deuteronomy 17:18-20). Israel neglected and
lost the Books at times (2 Chronicles 34:14-21), but God preserved them even through neglect, war, and exile.
The original Books were directly inspired by God and thus were perfect. A few errors occurred in copying.
In Hebrew, differences between numbers were sometimes shown by only the addition of a dot or two or a slight
variation in a line. A copyist could easily mistake one for the other, especially on worn scrolls. When comparing
Hebrew copies, the Targums in Aramaic and the Septuagint in Greek, no disagreement in essentials is found.
Most convincing proof that our present Old Testament is a trustworthy copy of the inspired original is the fact
that Jesus used, quoted, and approved of it (Luke 24:27, Luke 24:44). God has ordained that His Word shall
not pass away.
Translations
About three hundred years before Christ, some Jews settled in Alexandria, Egypt. As their children learned
Greek, they needed a Bible in that language. About 285 B.C. the Septuagint Version (means seventy) was
translated from Hebrew into Greek. This is the Bible that Jesus used.
When the Jews were captives in Babylon, they gradually learned to speak Aramaic. When the Hebrew Bible
was read, the meaning would be given orally in Aramaic (or Chaldee). Later these translations were written and
called Targums (meaning translations).
In the first six hundred years after Christ, some Jews spent their lives in copying the Old Testament Books to
get the most perfect complete Old Testament possible. These men were called Masoretes (meaning to hand
down). They took great pains to have every letter perfect.
Translations were made by different people from different manuscripts into many languages, including the
Gospel of John in English. In A.D.1380 in England, John Wycliffe finished translating the whole Bible from
the Latin Vulgate into English. This is the Wycliffe Version. All was done by hand. For opening the Bible to the
people, Roman priests had him arrested.
In A.D.1456 printing was developed in Germany. Now copying the Bible was less difficult. But translating
and distributing it was opposed by the Roman Catholic powers. In 1527 William Tyndale began to translate the
Old Testament. Before he could finish, he was imprisoned, strangled, and burned at the stake. Soon after came
the Coverdale Bible, edited by Myles Coverdale. Matthew's Bible was made by John Rogers. He combined
Tyndale's translation and Coverdale's. For his work, he was burned alive in 1555 in the persecution under the
Catholic "Bloody Queen Mary."
In 1604 King James I approved the making of a new version to silence discord over current versions. Much
of the influence and beauty of Tyndale's and Coverdale's work is seen in it. It was published in 1611 as the King
James Version. This remains the best and most-used English version.
JUST A THOUGHT
"Great souls have fed on great spiritual food." 

LESSON 4
WHAT THE NEW TESTAMENT IS
Scripture Texts: Matthew 1:1; Matthew 26:26-29; Mark 14:49;
Matthew 16:18-19; Acts 1:8-9; Romans 1:11-12; 2 Peter 3:18
The New Testament is twenty-seven Books in five groups. Each
of the four Gospels is named for the writer. All tell the story of Jesus'
life, yet each with a little different view. Matthew wrote, showing
Jesus to be the Jews looked-for Messiah and King. Mark wrote and
showed Jesus as the Servant of the Lord, beginning with John
preparing His way, His baptism, and moved with swift action through the episodes of His life. Luke wrote of
Jesus as the Son of man, stressing His human side. His Book begins with the birth of John and Jesus and gives
much detail throughout. John's Gospel is somewhat different. It contains deep spiritual thought. John wrote,
proving Jesus to be the Son of God. Much is told of Jesus' birth, death, and resurrection. His life is our example,
but His death is our salvation. By it, He provided the perfect sacrifice for sin. His resurrection made effective
His death and assured our resurrection.
The New Testament is the good news of salvation from sin through Christ, the calling out of the church, and
full victory to come.
MEMORY VERSE: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.—John 17:17
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Mark 16 Resurrection and ascension of Christ.
Tue.—Acts 14 Missionary work of Paul and Barnabas.
Wed.—James 4 Exhortations to the church.
Thu.—Revelation 21 A description of the church.
Fri.—Psalm 119:33-48 A prayer to delight in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 2 Teaching the church by letter.
A New Covenant
Matthew 1:1 The book of the generation of Jesus Christ. "Generation" here means birth, the entering into
human life. Christ was always divine. He is from everlasting to everlasting, but He had to take on humanity. The
process of His doing so is His generation. It is expressed in His name Emmanuel, meaning God with us
(Matthew 1:23). He was the eternal God come to live with us, to be one of us. Why are the names of David and
Abraham singled out? Because promises were given to them which Christ's coming fulfilled. A son of David
was to sit upon the throne of David (Isaiah 9:7; Luke 1:32). To Abraham God said, In thee shall all families
of the earth be blessed (Genesis 12:3).
Matthew 26:26-29 The purpose of Jesus' birth was that He might die—die to redeem mankind. In dying, He
sealed the new covenant with His blood. He gave bread and grape juice as symbols of that covenant. This is my
body . . . this is my blood of the new testament (or new covenant). The old covenant was also sealed by blood,
blood of animals (Exodus 24:3-8). The New Testament is so named because in it God's new testament of grace
is set forth—not on stone, but written on the heart. With this He began to set up the spiritual kingdom over
which He would rule forever. Until . . . I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.
Prophecies Must Be Fulfilled
Mark 14:49 But the scriptures must be fulfilled. The Old Testament had to be fulfilled if God's Word was
to be everlasting. The Old is promise, the New, fulfillment. The New was not yet written when Jesus was on
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.
What The New Testament Is─Lesson4
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 4
earth. When it says He did things that it might be fulfilled which was spoken, it refers to Old Testament
promises.
The Kingdom Set Up and Empowered
Matthew 16:18-19 Jesus said, I will build my church. In all of His work, He was gathering material for
His church. He was setting up His kingdom. From the first, He preached the gospel of the kingdom of God
(Mark 1:14; Luke 16:16). The New Testament is a record of the birth, growth, activity, nourishment, and
future hope of God's peculiar people, the antitype of Israel, His peculiar treasure under the old covenant
(1Peter 2:9; Exodus 19:5). Jesus said, I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven (or Kingdom
of God) to use on earth. It would be foolish to believe that Christ would give Peter keys to a kingdom that did
not exist.
Acts 1:8 Moving on into Acts, we read of Jesus' ascension back to Heaven and His promise: Ye shall
receive power from the Holy Ghost. Who was to come upon them? The result is Ye shall be witnesses unto
me—unto Jesus—in all the world. The Book of Acts is the record of that power and witnessing. The Holy Spirit
did come (Acts 2) and filled saints went forth as He led. This was the church going forth to build His kingdom.
The Acts is a history book written by Luke. It takes up the story where his Gospel left off. It is an account of
the progress of the church from the ascension of Christ and descent of the Holy Spirit to Paul's imprisonment in
Rome. It is the history of the spreading of the Gospel and planting churches amid miracles and persecution in
Jerusalem and Palestine, Asia Minor, and Europe. The conversion and work of Paul figures largely. It teaches
what God expects His church to be.
Paul's Epistles
Romans 1:11 Now come the letters of Paul to the churches. How were new converts to apply their new
knowledge and experience to their lives? To explain doctrine and instruct in Christian living, Paul wrote
thirteen, and possibly all, of these letters. (Hebrews is unsigned.) They are named for the churches or individuals
to whom they were sent. They are rich in spiritual food. Paul expresses his deep desire: That I may impart
unto you some spiritual gift, that he might take of the living water in his heart (John 4:10, John 4:14; Acts
9:17) and plant it in theirs to spring up and flow out in rivers of living water (John 7:37-39). Why? That ye
may be established, be rooted and built up in Christ (Colossians 2:7). This is provided as we study his letters.
2 Peter 3:18 These are the General Letters or Epistles. They were written for the same purpose, to help
saints to grow in grace—in the use of the power of God made available for our lives, and in the knowledge of
our Lord—getting to know Him by living in Him.
The Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ to John of the things that the church would go through from
its birth until Jesus comes back to receive it to Himself. It tells of the many enemies of the church, its battles and
great victories. In Revelation 22:20 Jesus says, Surely I come quickly. John looked forward to this. Amen.
Even so, come, Lord Jesus. Are you ready?

What The New Testament Is─Lesson4
www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 5
HOW THE NEW TESTAMENT CAME TO US
Scripture Texts: Colossians 4:16; 2 Peter 1:1; 2 Peter 1:12-15
The New Testament was written in Greek. For people of other
tongues to read it, it had to be translated into their languages. Some
languages possess many versions, and more than twelve hundred
languages possess at least part of the Bible. Still others have none of it.
God gave the Bible. He desires all men to hear it, commanded that it
be preached in all the world, and plants in the hearts of the saints a desire
to tell it. He says it will never be destroyed but will accomplish the
purpose for which it is sent. He exhorts us to search the Scriptures and to have His Words abiding in us. He has
used His Word to bless and save millions. He will not allow it to be brought to an end. He is watching to guard
against its destruction or corruption. We must do the same.
The New Testament is to stand forever and is to be passed on to all people for their salvation and spiritual
nurture.
MEMORY VERSE: And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou
to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.—2 Timothy 2:2
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 7:37-46 Jesus cries His invitation to all.
Tue.—John 21:15-22 Christ's sheep must be fed.
Wed.—Acts 4:1-22 Apostles' passion for telling the news.
Thu.—1 Corinthians 9:16-27 Paul's passion to preach Gospel.
Fri.—Psalm 119:49-64 David's trust in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: 2 Timothy 2:1-10 Word is to be passed on.
Congregations Shared the Epistles
Colossians 4:16 Paul wrote this letter from his prison cell to the church at Colosse (Colossians 4:18). He
tells them to cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans. Also, ye likewise read the epistle
from Laodicea. (Not written from there, but brought from there for reading.) Churches copied and kept the
precious letters. They were written to be shared.
2 Peter 1:1 Peter wrote to the church in general—to them that have obtained like precious faith. Other
books are addressed to saints generally: James—to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad; 1 Peter—to
the strangers scattered throughout named areas; Jude—to them that are sanctified. Hebrews 3:1—Holy
brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling. Christ gave The Revelation to shew unto his servants . . . 1
Corinthians—with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ; 2 Corinthians—with all the
saints which are in all Achaia; Ephesians—and to the faithful in Christ Jesus. Three of the Gospels were
recorded unaddressed for whosoever will to read. These show God's constant purpose to send His Word to all
mankind. He puts His power behind its preservation and spread.
Plans for Preserving the Scriptures
2 Peter 1:12-15 Peter intended to put the church in remembrance of the need of diligent obedience to
Christ. He did so even though the saints knew this and were established in the present truth—the level of truth
given men in this present dispensation. He knew, from his own experience, how easy it is to fall (Matthew
26:69-75). Peter must continually remind each one as long as I am in this tabernacle—while I live in this

temporary body. Shortly I must put off this my tabernacle—die. How did he know? Our Lord Jesus Christ
hath shewed me. But Peter's purpose of teaching God's Word reached beyond his death. I will endeavour that
ye may be able after my decease to have these things—teachings, truths—always in remembrance. He
preserved them in writing. No doubt, copies were made to keep in several safe places. Now over nineteen
hundred years later we have Peter's letters. Other writers carried out God's plan to hand down their letters for our
spiritual nutrition.
The Cost of Bringing the Bible to Us
Jerome spent twenty-one years in a monastery at Bethlehem translating a Greek Old Testament and an Old
Latin New Testament to make the Latin Vulgate Bible. Some copies were brought to England for use of church
leaders. The Christian king, Alfred the Great, who ruled from 871 to 901, encouraged righteousness and began
his list of laws with the Ten Commandments and other Bible selections. After a long time, John Wycliffe
translated the Bible from the Vulgate into Middle English, finishing in 1382. A group of men called Lollards
(poor priests) copied Wycliffe's Bible and walked about England reading it to the people and teaching them to
obey it.
After printing was invented, William Tyndale went to Germany to be free to translate and print the Bible.
His first New Testaments, printed in English, reached England by smuggling in bags of grain and bolts of cloth
in 1526. When strangled and burned in 1536, his last words were, "Lord, open the King of England's eyes."
Three years later King Henry VIII ordered that English Bibles be used in churches. Seventy years later King
James I ordered that a new translation be made. It was finished in 1611 and is the King James Version in use
today in England, America, and elsewhere. Copies were placed in church buildings, sometimes chained to a
desk where people came to read.
For translating the Bible, Wycliffe was arrested. His Bible was forbidden to the people. Church leaders
severely punished them for owning, reading, memorizing, or teaching the Bible in English. Some paid the
equivalent of $400 for a copy of it or a load of hay for a few chapters or for the privilege of reading it for a day.
Years after his death, Wycliffe's body was dug up, burned, and the ashes strewed on the River Swift. Think of
the long days and years spent in copying each Bible by hand, of the weary miles walked by the Lollards, and of
the courage required of many to keep on in spite of persecution. A whole printing of Tyndale's Bible was
publicly burned by order of the Bishop of London. Tyndale was put to death when only 44. This is but a small
part of the cost of bringing the Bible to us. Yet it lies on the shelf in many homes, dusty and unread. Are we
using it and obeying it as God intended? What of the future? Will it ever be a crime here to own and use a
Bible?
JUST A THOUGHT
When we do what we can do, God
will do what we cannot do.

LESSON 6
THE CHARACTER OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Matthew 24:35; 2 Timothy 3:16-17; 2 Peter 1:21; John
God has established methods by which He communicates with His
creation, man, to tell him His will. Some of His methods are through
nature, by direct speaking, by Christ, by the Holy Spirit, and through the
Bible.
Nature speaks of God's power and majesty, but it cannot tell us who He
is, whether He loves us, whether He will answer prayer, what the future
holds, what our duty is, or anything of grace and atonement. We may see
God in nature, but we cannot reach Him there. (Read Psalm 19:1-3.) God's most universal and plain
communication with man is the Bible.
We have seen the important position occupied by the Church of God. If it is to fill its place in God's plan, we
must know what God's will is. God has given us a Book which contains all we need to know to be saved and to
do His will on earth. This Book is the Bible. What is it like?
MEMORY VERSE: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.—Matthew 24:35
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Kings 8:54-61 Solomon's benediction.
Tue.—2 Timothy 3:10-17 The defense of the faith.
Wed.—2 Peter 1:12-21 The basis of true knowledge.
Thu. — 1 Corinthians 2:6-16 True wisdom the gift of God.
Fri.—John 12:44-50 A summary of Jesus' claims.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 19:7-14 The works and Word of God.
It Is Eternal
Matthew 24:35 My words shall not pass away. It is God's Word. It is inspired by God. It is true. The
world and all in it was brought into being by the power of His Word. There hath not failed one word of all his
good promise (1 Kings 8:56). God's Word was before this world came into being and will stand sure after it has
gone. His Word can never be destroyed because it is true.
The Bible Is Equipment for Christian Work
2 Timothy 3:16 All scripture is given by inspiration of God. Paul here refers to the Old Testament
Scriptures, but this may be applied to the New as well. The Bible sets forth eternal principles which could have
been conceived only by God. Its message fits any age of the world. If obeyed from the heart, it will produce a
new and clean character inside and out.
It is profitable for doctrine—it contains the doctrine of God which is the rule and standard of our faith.
Any doctrine which cannot be proved by the Bible is not required of man to accept. It is the last court of appeal
for religious doctrine. For reproof—it will reprove and rebuke the sinful life. It holds a high standard of moral
living. For correction—The Bible is profitable in restoring every person to his proper place in life. It will
correct our attitude and conduct if they are out of order. For instruction in righteousness—we need no creed
books or discipline books to guide us into the rules of faith and practice. The Word is sufficient. The Scriptures
were written for our learning and instruction, that we might know the will of God for us (Romans 15:4).

2 Timothy 3:17 That the man of God—saved people, saints—may be perfect—perfect in purity, clean,
sinless—and thoroughly furnished unto all good works. Read Ephesians 2:10. God's Book is fitted to carry
out His plan. We need the Book if we are to work the plan.
The Bible Is Inspired
2 Peter 1:21 Moved by the Holy Ghost—The Old Testament Prophets spoke as the Holy Ghost came upon
them. The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue (2 Samuel 23:2). This is
inspiration. It is the method by which our Bible came to us.
The very Words of the Bible came from God. They were only written down by man. No other book is like
the Bible. No other is inspired by God, or comes from God directly. Inspiration is the Holy Spirit putting into a
man's mind and heart the Words to say or write. Prophecy (God's Word to man) came not in old time by the
will of man: but holy men of God spake . . . moved by the Holy Ghost. This is God's way of giving our Bible
to us. Over and over, the Bible claims to be God's Word. This fact puts the obligation upon us to accept and
obey it.
Jesus put His stamp of approval on the whole Old Testament, all the Bible that was written at that time. The
Jews included all of it in the three divisions Jesus mentioned. He said, all things must be fulfilled, which were
written in the law . . . prophets . . . psalms (Luke 24:27, Luke 24:44). If Jesus says they are true, we can be
sure of them. While Jesus was with His disciples, He had pointed in the Old Testament to predictions
concerning Himself. Now that He has been crucified and resurrected, He assures them again that their faith in
Him as the Messiah might be strengthened, that all things concerning Him must be fulfilled (Luke 24:44).
The Bible Is Life-Giving
John 6:63 The words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life. The message of Jesus (and
the Gospel as a whole) has a spiritual application, and the fleshly mind cannot comprehend it without the spirit
of understanding given by the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:14). It is the Spirit of life that is in Christ Jesus that
brings salvation to us and not the letter of the Law. We may be strict adherents to the letter of the Word and not
have the Spirit within our hearts, and it would profit us nothing. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ,
he is none of his (Romans 8:9).
The Bible was given to us to use. In it, we find statements of truth, warning when we stray, a standard to
measure us and bring us back to the right way, and a teacher of God's will. It is to furnish us thoroughly unto all
good works. No one, however educated and trained otherwise, is capable of doing God's work unless the Bible
is in his heart and mind and hand. This does not mean leaders only, but all of us who have been created in
Christ Jesus unto good works (Ephesians 2:10). All are to spread the Gospel. Shall the whole beautiful,
eternal plan of God come to an end, fail, when it reaches us, just because we do not read, study, eat, and obey
His Word, the Bible? It is tragic that just that is happening in many lives.
The Bible Will Judge Us
John 12:48 The word that I have spoken . . . shall judge . . . Christ and His Word (doctrine) are one and
inseparable. If we reject the message of His Word, we have rejected Him. It is impossible to have the Spirit of
Christ dwelling in us and reject the Word. His Word and doctrine will be the standard of judgment on that final
day.

LESSON 7
PROPHECIES OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Deuteronomy 18:22; Isaiah 34:16; 1 Peter 1:10-12
The Prophets did not understand all they spoke. They looked for the
fulfillment of the prophecy but never lived to see it fulfilled. But they
believed it would come to pass. They wondered what it was and when it would come. This was puzzling because
they had the prediction only. The things they prophesied in their time are being fulfilled in this Gospel
dispensation through Jesus.
Prophecy is not true, does not come to pass because it is written in the Bible, but it is in the Bible because it
is true and will come to pass. Every prophecy of the Bible has so far been fulfilled. This is one of the strongest
proofs of the truth of the Bible. No prophecy shall lack its fulfillment. We find fulfilled prophecies all through
the New Testament.
MEMORY VERSE: Behold, the former things are come to pass, and new things do I declare: before they
spring forth I tell you of them.—Isaiah 42:9
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 18:15-22 The true Prophet promised.
Tue.—Isaiah 46:5-13 The end from the beginning.
Wed.—Ezekiel 12:21-28 God's Word shall be done.
Thu.—Daniel 2:24-30 God revealeth secrets.
Fri.—Psalm 119:65-80 Praising God for keeping His Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 42:1-9 God tells of events ahead.
True Prophecies Come to Pass
Deuteronomy 18:22 When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord—claims to speak for the Lord, to
tell what God has told him. There were false prophets then as well as now. How can one tell the false from the
true? If the thing follow not—if his saying does not come true, does not come to pass—then the Lord hath
not spoken it. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously—without authority, without Word from God. Thou
shalt not be afraid of him, shall not believe or observe his words. Implied here is the fact that prophecies which
the Lord HAS spoken do come to pass, do occur just as spoken. No one is really a prophet unless God has
spoken the message to him. We have a good example of this is 2 Samuel 18:19-31.
Jeremiah prophesied the captivity and death of Zedekiah, king of Judah (Jeremiah 34:1-7). The people
accused him of disloyalty and put him in jail (Jeremiah 37:11-15, 28). But this (and other things) happened just
as Jeremiah prophesied (Jeremiah 52:1-12). He spoke what God had spoken to him.
No Word of God Shall Fail
Isaiah 34:16 Seek ye out of the book of the Lord and read. Read the promises, warnings, and predictions.
No one of these shall fail. This is God's pledge. For every promise, there must be its matching fulfillment.
Why? Because God's mouth it hath commanded. His Word cannot fail. His spirit it hath gathered them—the
Spirit of God has gathered the Words, the people, and events together to bring the fulfillment. No Word of the
Bible has ever been found false. God said He would bring all His Words to pass (Ezekiel 12:28).

Old Testament Prophecies of New Testament Salvation
1 Peter 1:10-12 The prophets have enquired and searched diligently. They did not understand the
meaning when they prophesied of the grace to come, so they enquired and searched for it. They wondered
what it was and what manner of time it would come. The Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify—
the Holy Spirit in their hearts made known these things. He testified beforehand—predicted— the sufferings
of Christ, and the glory . . . For example, Isaiah wrote seven hundred years before Christ was born that He was
despised . . . rejected . . . a man of sorrows . . . wounded . . . bruised . . . oppressed . . . afflicted . . . brought
as a lamb to the slaughter . . . and was cut off out of the land of the living. All this for our iniquities. Then,
in contrast, is the glory, that he shall see his seed . . . prolong his days . . . the pleasure of the Lord shall
prosper in his hand . . . he shall be satisfied and divide the spoil with the strong (Isaiah 53). Puzzling,
certainly, to one who has the prediction only. God answered their inquiries by revealing that they did minister
the things . . . not unto themselves—the prophecies were not to be fulfilled in their time—but unto us in the
next, this Gospel dispensation. The things they prophesied have come to pass and are reported by Spirit-led
preachers of the gospel. They tell of Christ's substitutionary death, His Resurrection, and of those saved and
Spirit-filled by His power. The prophecies of the old dispensation of Law are fulfilled in the new dispensation of
grace. The angels are shut out from these blessings of salvation. They can only desire to look into them. They
are precious to the angels, but only those who repent and believe can partake of it. Seek it, receive it, keep it, and
tell of it.

We can trust His promise to come again—John 14:3; Acts 1:10-11. These prophecies were given from
seven hundred to a thousand years before Christ was born. That they could come true by chance is an absolute
impossibility. No one man could by chance fulfill all these prophecies and more. Some of them no one not
divine could ever fulfill. There is but one answer— the prophecies are from God, the Book is God's Book.
JUST A THOUGHT
There have always been unbelievers in God and His
Word, but none have ever brought forth any proof.

LESSON 8
JESUS AND THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Hebrews 1:1-2; Luke 24:44: Matthew 5:17-18; John 6:63
The Gospels are biographies of Jesus. Acts is an account of the Spirit-led witness
to Him by His church. The Epistles are records and explanations of His teachings. The
Revelation is His showing forth of His plan for man from the beginning of the Gospel
dispensation to eternity. Every Book of the Bible speaks of Jesus by promise or type
or symbol or statement of fact.
Jesus is the central figure of the whole Bible. The Old Testament looks forward to
Him; the New Testament looks back to Him. Both exalt Him. It is accurate to say
Jesus "believed" the Bible. It originated with Him. Jesus recommends the Bible to be
trustworthy when He quotes it, fulfills its prophecies, and tells us to search the Scriptures.
MEMORY VERSE: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which
testify of me. ─John 5:39
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 5:36-47 Moses wrote of Christ.
Tue.—John 6:51-63 We must eat the Words of Christ.
Wed.—1 Timothy 6:3-14 God's Word is the foundation.

Fri.—Psalm 119:81-96 Choosing God's Word in trouble.

Jesus Is the Living Bible
Hebrews 1:1-2 In time past—in the former dispensation— God spoke unto the fathers by the prophets.
In 2 Kings 17:13, we read that the Lord testified against Israel, or gave them no excuse, by all the prophets
. . . saying, Turn ye from your evil ways, and keep my commandments . . . according to all the law which I
commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets. The Prophets gave
warnings, promises, teachings, commands, guidance, and foretelling of events. But now in these last days— the
last dispensation of time—God has spoken unto us by his Son—Jesus Christ.
The Bible opens with the account of Creation, and the Hebrew word for God in Genesis 1:1 is plural (Gods).
Jesus, together with His Father and the Spirit, created all things (Colossians 1:16). By whom also he made the
worlds (Hebrews 1:2). He is the One promised to bruise the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15) and to bless the
world through Abraham (Genesis 12:3). He is the Prophet promised to Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15). He is
pictured as the Passover Lamb (Exodus 12). He is typified in Isaac, Joseph, Moses, Joshua, David, and others.
The Psalms have many prophetic references to Jesus. For example, Psalm 96. The Books of Prophecy promise
His coming—Behold, the Lord God will come . . . He shall feed his flock like a shepherd (Isaiah 40:10-11).
God has always communicated with man. Prophets brought His message. Some obeyed, but more did not.
Then God began His better plan, a new dispensation. He sent His best message, His Son Jesus Christ. Jesus is
called the Word in John 1:1 and John 1:14— the Word was God . . . the Word was made flesh, and dwelt
among us—and in 1 John 1:1-2, That which was from the beginning, which we have heard . . . seen . . .

And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God. God gave us
His written Law that is powerful, and then His living Word Who is more powerful. The written Word shows us
His will. The living Word gives us power to obey it. By His written Word, He comes to us. By His living Word,

LESSON 9
THE PURPOSE OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: Psalm 102:12-28; Romans 1:14; Romans 16:25-26
Law, history, wisdom, drama, guidance—these are some things the Bible
brings to mankind. We have learned that the Prophet was sometimes a
foreteller, but more often a forthright preacher.
From the very beginning, there has been a deep yearning for God in the heart of man. God has placed within
His written Word, the Bible, direction for man, which, if followed, will lead him from his self-centered life to a
soul-satisfying, God-centered life in Christ. Heart highways that lead to Zion! Roads over which God can march
into the strongholds of our hearts. The Bible brings down into our daily walk the God Who made the earth and
stars and Who keeps the planets in their orbits. He Who in the beginning said, "Let there be light," also speaks
the same Word to the darkness of our lives. Jesus, Who wept at the grave of Lazarus, enters into our sorrows
still.
MEMORY VERSE: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy
word.—Psalm 119:9
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 4:1-9 Passing on God's Word as it is.
Tue.—Nehemiah 8 Ezra reads God's Law to the people.
Wed.—Luke 8:4-15 Sowing the seed.

Good News to All People
Psalm 102 This chapter begins with a great cry of distress. In Psalm 102:12 the writer turns to consider
God, and hope mounts. He begins to prophesy as God speaks through him of the coming of Christ. He shall
appear (Psalm 102:16) bringing salvation to loose those that are appointed to death (Psalm 102:20). He sets
his own weakness and shortness of life beside God's strength and endlessness, then shows God's people so
closely unified with God as to partake of His eternity (Psalm 102:27-28).
Psalm 102:18-22 This shall be written for the generation to come. God revealed that this good news was
to be passed on by the written word. Future generations would read and praise the Lord. Why? Because the
Lord would look down from his sanctuary; from heaven, see the needy earth, and hear the groaning of the
prisoner—prisoners of Satan bound by the prison bars of sin. Why would He look? To loose those that are
appointed to death—to save them from hell. This is the Gospel written beforehand, a picture of the love of God
for lost sinners. It was to be delivered to mankind without change to reconcile man and God (2 Corinthians
5:18-19). It was to be proclaimed from Zion and Jerusalem (Micah 4:2; Luke 24:47). Zion, near Jerusalem, was
the city of David the king (1 Chronicles 11:5) and was a type of the church (Isaiah 35:10). People and
kingdoms would be gathered together . . . to serve the Lord. People cannot be pulled or driven together. They
must flow together (Isaiah 2:2). The Prophet here foretells the establishing of God's church, the mountain of
the Lord's house. It shall be exalted above the hills. Centuries later, Christ was to liken His disciples to a city
that is set on a hill which cannot be hid (Matthew 5:14). And all nations shall flow unto it. Metal cannot be
pulled or forced together. The cold, hard hearts of men from all nations, both Jews and Gentiles, are made into
one people by the heat of the Holy Spirit melting their hearts together into one people through salvation.
Micah had no faith in any remedy except God. His message was that when men turn to God, they will have
peace; when they give up oppression, they will have prosperity. It has always been man's belief that he can

manage his own affairs without any reference to the will and purpose of God. God knew there was no solution

We Owe the Gospel to All People

The Gospel Opened to All
Romans 16:25-26 The preaching of Jesus Christ was the revelation of the mystery of God's plan to save
sinners. His plan was a mystery because it was kept secret since the world began. When Christ came, it was
made manifest, revealed. It was made known to all nations . . . by the scriptures of the prophets. These Old
Testament Scriptures foretelling salvation in Christ were preached by the Apostles (Acts 13:14-41). It was by
the commandment of the everlasting God that the Gospel was opened to all nations. It remains for His
servants to carry it to them. Jesus gave this command just before leaving this world (Matthew 28:19-20; Acts
1:8). We cannot teach Christ unless we have Him. No unsaved person can teach the way to God.
JUST A THOUGHT
Knowledge is one thing that does not become
secondhand when used.

LESSON 10
THE BIBLE IS INSPIRED
Scripture Texts: Galatians 1:11-12; 2 Timothy 3:15-17; 2 Peter 1:20-21
What is meant by inspiration? The word means "a breathing in." God's
breath, or His life, is upon the Words of the Bible. We may read the Bible, but
unless we are inspired by the Holy Spirit, it will be only empty words without
spiritual life. The breath of the Almighty is on it and in it. It is an authority of
truth higher than the authority of the mind.
In 2 Timothy, the Bible lays claim to divine inspiration. Every believing
man or woman who has taken this statement at its face value has been brought
into a rich, firm experience in spiritual growth.
MEMORY VERSE: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for
correction, for instruction in righteousness:—2 Timothy 3:16
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—2 Samuel 23:1-7 David claimed inspiration.
Tue.—Galatians 1:1-17 Paul taught the inspired Gospel.
Wed.—Galatians 2:1-9 Apostles recognized Paul's inspiration.
Thu.—1 Peter 1:1-12 The Spirit of Christ inspired prophecy.
Fri.—Psalm 119:97-112 David’s love for God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 3:1-12 Paul taught by the Spirit.
Paul's Claim to Inspiration
Galatians 1:11-12 I certify—what Paul is about to say is sure and certain. The gospel which was preached
of me is not after man—not of man's thinking. Neither was I taught it— not learned from human teachers—
but by the revelation of Jesus Christ—it was revealed to him by Jesus. Paul's knowledge in the mystery of
Christ was received by revelation (Ephesians 3:2-5). Jesus promised this when He appeared to Paul on the
road to Damascus (Acts 26:16).
A small part of the Bible—the Ten Commandments—God Himself wrote (Exodus 31:18; Exodus 32:16).
Other parts, He spoke (Exodus 25:1; Jeremiah 30:2; Revelation 2:1). Still other parts were written as the Holy
Spirit took control of the thoughts of a man (Ephesians 1:17-18).
Inspiration is not revelation, but revelation is inspiration. Revelation is that act of God by which He directly
communicates truth not known before. Examples of revealed truth are 1 Corinthians 15 and 1 Thessalonians 4,
the future resurrection; 1 Timothy 4:1-3, the coming apostasy; and the visions in the Book of Revelation. Not
all Scripture needed to be revealed. Some was already known. But all, both the revealed and the known, were
inspired. Inspiration is the guidance of the Holy Spirit in telling or writing of truth already revealed (Job 32:8).
The Bible records both sins and right acts, sayings of Satan and sayings of God. Not all were inspired when
done or said. But the RECORD of them is inspired and true. The Holy Spirit selected the writer and the matter to
be written and directed in the writing.
All Sacred Scripture Inspired
2 Timothy 3:15-17 The Holy Scriptures which Timothy knew are the Old Testament Books. In
recommending them, Paul says All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable . . . The
writings given to Israel for their guidance and which they gathered together and looked upon as God's Word, are
the same as our Old Testament upon which Jesus put His approval. These were called the Scriptures or Holy
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.

LESSON 10
Scriptures (John 5:39; Romans 1:2; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4). Because they are inspired by God, they are true
and are profitable. For what? Doctrine—for teaching God's will, Jesus Christ, and the way to be saved.
Reproof—to warn sinners of the result if they do not repent. Correction—a standard to bring men back to true
doctrine and the right way, as they have a tendency to go astray. Instruction in righteousness—to give
knowledge of God, His ways, and how to please Him. These are to make the man of God—any who belongs to
Him—perfect and thoroughly furnished. Everything is furnished that is needed for a perfect life in Christ. No
one is furnished or trained or educated for the good life without knowledge of and belief in the Bible (Proverbs
Sometimes the word inspired is mistakenly applied to a song, poem, or writing not in the Bible. There is a
difference between a divine revelation of the mind of God and a divine action on the mind of man. The former is
revelation; the latter is spiritual enlightenment or inspiration. We hear it said, "I did not see this before. I am
going to walk in this light." That truth has been revealed for centuries, but it just became light or truth to you by
the Holy Spirit's inspiration. The Bible is God's public revelation; what He says to us in our daily, private
worship is for us and for our needs. God speaks to us through the Bible, prayer, worship, and the conscience.
Both individuals and nations are enlightened by its use.
The Holy Spirit Gave the Word
2 Peter 1:20-21 No prophecy of the scripture—no God-given message—is of any private interpretation.
We must not give it OUR meaning but let the Giver interpret it for us. The prophecy came not . . . by the will
of man. We must go to the One with authority. If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God (James 1:5).
Holy men of God spake . . . moved by the Holy Ghost. This spoken of the Old Testament is equally true of the
New. New Testament preachers preached with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven. They also wrote it (1
Peter 1:12). Two agents here—holy men and the Holy Ghost. He moved them—stirred their desires and
guided their thoughts. They wrote as He guided. The Lord gave the word (Psalm 68:11). This is God's way of
preserving His Word against destruction.
Those things which we cannot understand, we are asked to accept on faith, and it has been the experience of
believers through the ages that when they manifest such faith, the things they could not honestly understand
either became clear to them or ceased to be a cause of anxiety and bewilderment.
We must beware of "cunningly devised fables," for such mislead the faithful today when men substitute their
own theories for the infallible Word of God.
JUST A THOUGHT
"The principles of the Bible are the groundwork
of human freedom."
