LESSON 11
THE BIBLE HAS POWER AND AUTHORITY
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 55:11; Luke 16:17; John 15:7;
Hebrews 4:12; Acts 20:32
The Bible bears the sovereign authority of God. It is true. It is powerful.
The Word of God is living and is active. It is the Book into which the all-
powerful, all-knowing, and all-loving God has breathed the breath of spiritual
life. When Jesus came, this powerful Word was made flesh, which dwelt
among us, full of grace and truth.
The whole world is sinking deeper every day into a lower level of spiritual illiteracy. Only the power and
authority of the Bible can lift it to a higher plain. But only as mankind reads and obeys its teachings will it have
a leveling effect upon a world that is sinking to tragic destruction.
MEMORY VERSE: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.—
Ephesians 6:17
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Jeremiah 23:18-32 — God’s Word versus false prophecies.
Tue.—Matthew 8:5-13 — The power of Christ's Words.
Wed.—Mark 7:1-13 — Human tradition is wrong.
Thu.—John 8:23-32 — Jesus spoke as His Father taught Him.
Fri.—Psalm 119:113-128 — David's hope in God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Isaiah 55 — God's Word shall fulfill His will.
God's Word Has Power to Succeed
Isaiah 55:11 My word . . . shall not return unto me void— not be without result—shall accomplish . . .
shall prosper. God put power into His Word. He links His Word with His purpose. I have spoken it, I will also
bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it (Isaiah 46:11).
Luke 16:17 Jesus expressed the certainty of God's Word to succeed. It is easier for heaven and earth to
pass, than one tittle of the law to fail. It cannot, for the authority of God is in it. Power comes from authority.
God has authority because He is Author of all things, so, greater than they. Read Mark 1:22. Not all who hear
the Word will accept it, but some will (Mark 4:14-20). His word was with power (Luke 4:32). Power to do
what? To carry out each Word. His power and authority came from God, His Father. Jesus was the Word which
became flesh and dwelt among them.
God's Word Gives Power in Prayer
John 15:7 If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you. Here is the power to unite man with God and to
bring into our lives all the power which God's Word affords us. For if we ask any thing according to his will,
he heareth us (1 John 5:14). Every promise in the Bible is ours. What unites them? (1) If ye abide in me—in
Christ, yielded to Him, dead to self, and alive in Christ (Colossians 3:3; Galatians 2:20). (2) If my words
abide in you—if you believe, obey, and love His Words until they are spirit and life in you (John 6:63), until
they lead to the living Word, Christ Jesus. The connection being made, God's Word is set in motion to answer
the prayer. Power comes from authority. The authority of God is in His Word.

LESSON 11
God's Word Has Power to Penetrate Hard Hearts
Hebrews 4:12 The word of God is quick—living. Powerful— can do God's will. Sharper than any two-
edged sword—no dull or ineffective edge. It divides between soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow—
pairs very nearly alike and hard to separate. They are used figuratively to express the power of the Bible to
penetrate. As a living thing, it is a discerner. It puts the finger on the very point where guilt or virtue has its
center in the heart. It sees through words to thoughts, past acts to intents. It points them out to us, convicting
and directing. For instance, it tells us hatred is murder (1 John 3:15), all sins begin in the heart (Mark 7:21-23),
and the Kingdom of God is entered only by spiritual birth (John 3:5).
This sharp, two-edged sword cuts to pieces our selfishness and sin. The Bible says no to many of our
cherished plans. It cuts deep into the customs of men. It puts a roadblock in front of fleshly passions. It bids us
to be merciful if we would receive mercy.
Praise God when it cuts down into your life, separating those things which tend to hold us back and take
away our liberty and freedom. Let the Bible criticize you before your conscience and the world get a chance to
do so.
God's Word Has Power to Save
Acts 20:32 I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace—the Bible, which ministers God's grace,
or a supply of His life. The Word is able to build you up—to give you knowledge, spiritual strength, faith. And
an inheritance among the sanctified—to give possessions which sanctified ones have— life, holiness, power,
love, faith, fruit of the Spirit, and a home in Heaven. One does not get these by having a Bible only, or reading it
only, or going through forms, or performing outward works. No, only by hearing, believing, and obeying is one
led to Christ Who saves (James 1:21-25). We must do the will of the Father (Matthew 7:21). The Bible shows
us His will.
In God's Word is the authority of God. For effective work that accomplishes God's will, we must use it.
When a child inquires, read with him the answer from the Bible. To lead the unsaved to Christ, use Scripture.
People need instructing, the church needs reviving, lives need changing, and problems need solving. There is
only one way to do this, and that is to stand in God's counsel and cause the people to hear His Words, seasoned
with prayer (Jeremiah 23:22).
All this power is unleashed by faith in God's Word. It is all rendered powerless by unbelief. Enemies of God
have always tried to take authority away from His Word, the Bible. Unbelief has taken various forms from the
time of Eden until now. Some are: (1) Atheism—denial of the existence of God. (2) Agnosticism— the doctrine
that one cannot know as to the nature of God, a future life, etc. (3) Infidelity—lack of faith, unbelief. It denies
the truth of the Bible and Christian teachings. (4) Higher Criticism— critical study of the Bible, aimed to find
faults within. The writers of the Bible were not its authors; the Holy Spirit was. The writers were put in trust
with the gospel (1 Thessalonians 2:3-4).
JUST A THOUGHT
Unbelievers are not convinced by factual evidence,
but by the Spirit's power working in a life.

LESSON 12
OUR USE OF THE BIBLE
Scripture Texts: 1Peter 2:2-3; Hebrews 5:12-14; Deuteronomy 6:6-7;
Luke 11:28; 2 Timothy 3:16-17
It is not enough to own a Bible. We must hunger for it, hunger to read
it, take it into our hearts. We cannot be hungry by trying. Start in and read
it. That helps. But the only way to complete your desire is told in 1 Peter
2:2-3—if you are saved. The taste of Jesus brings hunger for His Word. As we hunger and read, the Holy Spirit
brings a greater understanding. When we read it with the God-given desire, we will grow thereby.
Since God gave us the Bible to use, it is our responsibility to use it. We must believe it, take it without
addition or subtraction, obey it, teach it to our children, and spread its message to all people. For us to use the
Bible, we must know it. If we do not use it correctly, we will lose it directly. Use it rightfully, and it is effective.
MEMORY VERSE: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.—Luke 11:28
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Deuteronomy 6:1-7 Teaching the Word at home.
Tue.—Amos 8:4-14 A famine of the Word.
Wed.—Hebrews 5:12-14 Progress from milk to meat.
Thu.—1 Peter 2:1-8 Only the saved grow by the Word.
Fri.—Psalm 119:161-176 The preciousness of God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Matthew 7:21-29 The wise obey God's Word.
Hunger for the Word
1 Peter 2:2-3 As newborn babes, desire . . . These are people who had been born again, quickened, or
made alive, by the Word. Being made alive by the Word, they need the Word to continue in this new life. As the
newborn infant requires milk for nourishment, so the newborn Christian needs the sincere milk of the word to
live thereby. As the natural baby's first desire is to find something to eat, so the newborn Christian will desire
the Word of God. However, we cannot desire of ourselves, and God does not ask us to. He plants the desire
when He saves and fills us with the Spirit. We cultivate the desire. He satisfies as we obey. The sincere milk—
the pure, unadulterated, plain teachings of God which are found in the Bible. That ye may grow . . . Milk
makes a baby grow. God's Word makes a soul grow wiser, stronger, more godly, more effectual in prayer, and
more able to be of service to God. If so be—a condition attached— that ye have tasted—experienced the
saving grace of the Lord, been born again. A baby must live before it can eat and grow. A soul must live
spiritually before it can eat and grow by the Word. A natural, or unsaved, one might read the Bible for years
and never grow (1 Corinthians 2:14). The order is: live, eat, grow.
Study the Word
Hebrews 5:12 Ye ought to be teachers. These Hebrews had heard the Gospel so many years and professed
to be followers of the Lord. They should know the truth and be capable of teaching it to others, but were still
children in understanding, unable to understand the deeper truths (meats). They still required milk (the primary
principles of the Word). Some people are ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the
truth (2 Timothy 3:7). They hear the Gospel, but not mixed with faith in them, it is to no avail. Read Romans
2:13; James 1:21-25. Under the same preaching, some will grow spiritually, while others die (1 Corinthians

LESSON 12
Hebrews 5:13 He is a babe—He who understands only the primary doctrines of the Gospel testifies that he
is only a babe (beginner) in Christ. Perhaps he has failed to study the Word and apply it to his life, or is dull of
hearing (Hebrews 5:11; Acts 28:27). We should diligently study God's Word and come to a mature
understanding of the deeper truths and not tarry with the primary doctrines such as repentance and faith.
Hebrews 5:14 Strong meat—The deeper, richer truths of God belong to the older saint rather than the
newborn because he has grown and matured. A baby cannot be expected to digest the same food as an older
person, neither should he be a baby forever. Those who by reason of use have their senses exercised— Those
who have searched its pages with a hungry and believing heart, have obeyed its commands, have grown to be
stalwart Christians, able to discern good from evil. Parents become concerned when a baby lacks growth and
proper development in due time. So should it cause concern when a babe in Christ fails to develop into more
than a spiritual bottle baby. Healthy babies grow up. Many have been deceived by some smooth-tongued,
would-be prophet because they failed to study the Word and so were unable to discern truth from error. Every
saint, whatever his place in the church, should be a teacher of the Bible.
Teach the Word in the Home
Deuteronomy 6:6-7 In thine heart—The Christian should prize the Word of God above all else. Like
David, we should hide it in our hearts (Psalm 119:11). If it be not in our hearts, it will profit us nothing. Thou
shalt teach . . . thy children. God commands Israel to teach His Word to their offspring. Christians should
consider the Bible the supreme Book of the home. Along with some other good books are many bad books.
They can influence and mislead, thus wrecking one's Christian life. With all diligence, patience, and
understanding, we should teach the Word to our children while they are young, that it may mold their lives as
they grow. The Word never returns empty (Isaiah 55:11). If received into the heart, it will save; if rejected, it
will damn.
Obey the Word
Luke 11:28 Jesus said, Yea rather, blessed are they— Some are more blessed than others. Blessed is the
mother who bore Jesus (Luke 11:27). More blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. This is
how much God values obedience. Not everyone that saith . . . but he that doeth the will of my Father . . .
The wise man whose house will not fall is whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them
(Matthew 7:21, Matthew 7:24). To fall short in obedience is to lose all.
Be Equipped With the Word
2 Timothy 3:16-17 All scripture . . . is profitable . . . throughly furnished . . . The end result of eating
food is strength to do. So, the end result of taking the Word of God is spiritual strength to do all good works.
Thus we are equipped to fill our place in the church. First, we must take His Word into our souls; then we can
give it out to others. No taking in, no giving out effectively.
Hands Off the Word
Revelation 22:18-19 If every commandment is observed fully, it will accomplish its purpose. I testify—
Jesus speaking—If any man shall add . . . God shall add . . . plagues . . . If any man take away . . . God shall
take away his part . . . It is a dangerous thing to tamper with the Bible. We are not to add to nor subtract from
it. To add to its precepts is to suffer the judgments of God; to diminish from it is to lose the blessings it offers.
We must handle the Bible with fear and reverence.

LESSON 13
THE BIBLE AT THE JUDGMENT
Scripture Texts: John 12:47-50; Romans 2:11-16; Revelation 20:12-15
We are all to be judged according to how our lives measure up to the Bible and
our attitude toward obeying its commandments.
Is there a more solemn thought than that we must stand and be judged by God?
He has told us the standard by which we will be judged. He has written it in a Book
and given us the Book. He has given the Holy Spirit to teach us His Word and
enlighten all that are born into the world. What is the wise course for us to take? Why
do some not take it? Saints have an obligation to acquaint others with the Bible.
MEMORY VERSE: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that
I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.—John 12:48
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ezekiel 13:1-14 False prophets to be punished.
Tue.—Mark 8:34-38 Must not be ashamed of Christ's Words.
Wed.—Romans 2:1-16 To be judged according to knowledge.
Thu.—1 Peter 3:9-18 Being ready for the Lord.
Fri.—Psalm 119:129-144 David's great longing for God's Word.
Devotional Reading: Revelation 22:12-21 Danger in changing God's Word.
Christ's Words Will Judge Us
John 12:47-48 I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. (See John 3:17.) Jesus came in love
for mankind. His foremost desire was to save sinners and bring them to Himself. He desired to make us a holy
family together here in this life, so we could be together in the next. But He cannot let down His holy standard.
His Word is changeless. He could not save if it were not. So if one rejects Him by receiving not His Words, he
puts himself under the condemnation of those Words. The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him
in the last day—the Day of Judgment, which is to come when all are resurrected as told in John 5:28-30. The
Words of God spoken to us now are a preliminary judgment of that which will be final then. If we cannot pass
the test as Christ's Word checks us out here, we can never hope to pass at the final Judgment. In the preliminary,
we have an opportunity to change it, but at the final Judgment, we have no chance of change.
Authority Behind Christ's Words
John 12:49-50 I have not spoken of myself. None of the Trinity speaks or works alone. They have perfect
unity. The Father . . . gave me a commandment . . . what I should speak. The authority of the Father is in
ALL the Words of Jesus—for whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak.
Jesus said, He that hath the Son hath life—to have His Word is to have Christ. God hath given to us eternal
life, and this life is in his Son (1 John 5:11-12). His salvation is a system of eternal life to bring the power of
God to dying, miserable man. It will not do man any good that he has believed that Christ has come in the flesh
to destroy the works of the devil if he does not come unto Him and receive life, but continues to live under the
power and guilt of sin.

LESSON 13
Judged According to the Gospel
Romans 2:11-15 As many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law—will perish, not
being born again. But their punishment will be less severe than of those who knew God's will and His offer of
salvation (Luke 12:47-48). Romans 2:14-15 tell us that the Gentiles—heathens—all have a law written in
their hearts, their conscience. This is the law these ones will be judged by. As many as have sinned in the
law—Moses' Law, knowing the law—shall be judged by the law— must measure to the requirements they knew
or be punished accordingly.
Romans 2:16 God shall judge the secrets of men. The inmost heart will be laid bare (Luke 12:2). By
Jesus Christ—He will be our Judge then, no more our Mediator (2 Corinthians 5:10). According to my
gospel—the Gospel Paul preached, the Gospel of Christ. The Gospel is the standard of judgment. Have you
received it? Have you loved to obey it? (1 John 5:3).
If those ignorant of God's Word will be beaten with few stripes (Luke 12:48), might it be better not to
know? But one without the Word and so, without Christ, must perish. Though his stripes be fewer, still they are
stripes. He is forever cut off from Christ and eternal life. It is best to know and to obey God's Word. Can one
plead ignorance by closing the Bible and refusing to read? No. To know where to find God's Word or even that
He gave a Word, is enough knowledge to make one accountable for knowing and obeying.
God's Books Will Measure Our Works
Revelation 20:12-15 And I saw the dead small, and great, stand before God . . . This is the final
Judgment of all people, the only Judgment the Bible tells of. . . . they were judged every man according to
their works. Two kinds of books are opened: (1) the books and (2) the book of life. The books are the standard
of measurement by which each is to be judged, for the dead were judged out of those things which were
written in the books. And also, according to their works. Our works—the thoughts, words, and deeds of our
lives—will be held beside the commands in the Books. They must agree. Their quality must measure to the
quality required. If so, we will pass the Judgment. If not, we will be lost forever—a great tragedy! These Books
are those which contain the Word Christ has spoken and the Gospel, the Bible. The other Book, the book of life,
lists the names of God's children, those who will pass the Judgment and enter Heaven. Our names must be
written in the book of life while we are in this world—before we die. It is written there when we are made alive
in Christ—saved, born again (Luke 10:20). Can you remember when your name was written in the pages of the
book of life?
JUST A THOUGHT
What are you doing with the Bible?
